MONDO:0003409.text: Pathological processes in the colon region of the large intestine (intestine, large).

MONDO:0003410.text: A cervical adenocarcinoma that arises from mesonephric remnants. It is usually characterized by the presence of tubular glands lined by cuboidal epithelial cells.

MONDO:0003411.text: A hemangiopericytoma arising from the breast.

MONDO:0003412.text: A benign or malignant hemangiopericytoma arising from the retroperitoneum.

MONDO:0003413.text: A benign or malignant neoplasm arising from the hair follicle.

MONDO:0003414.text: A very rare, locally aggressive, malignant neoplasm of the hair follicle. The majority of the cases arise de novo, however malignant transformation from a pre-existing pilomatricoma has been reported. It usually presents as a solitary nodule in the head and neck, upper extremities, or buttocks. Morphologically, it is characterized by the presence of aggregates of basaloid cells infiltrating the dermis. Masses of ghost cells are present in the cellular aggregates. Complete surgical excision is the treatment of choice. If it is not completely removed, it usually recurs, but it rarely metastasizes to distant anatomic sites.

MONDO:0003419.text: A rare, benign neoplasm that arises from the Bartholin gland and is characterized by the presence of clustered glands and tubules lined by mucin-secreting epithelial cells.

MONDO:0003420.text: An epithelial, usually multiloculated neoplasm arising from the intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts. It occurs predominantly in females. Signs and symptoms include abdominal mass, abdominal pain, and jaundice. Morphologically, the cystic spaces are lined by columnar epithelium and contain mucinous or serous fluid.

MONDO:0003421.text: An adenoma characterized by the presence of a mixed epithelial cell population.

MONDO:0003422.text: A benign, well circumscribed epithelial neoplasm that arises from the bronchus or the lung parenchyma. Representative examples include alveolar adenoma, papillary adenoma, and mucus gland adenoma.

MONDO:0003424.text: A benign neoplasm composed of large cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm. Representative examples include oncocytic adenomas of the thyroid gland, parathyroid gland, and pituitary gland.

MONDO:0003425.text: Weakness or paralysis of at least one of the muscles controlling the movement of the eye. It results from degeneration of the muscles or the neural pathways involved in the eye movement. Representative disorders causing ophthalmoplegia include ocular myopathies and multiple sclerosis.

MONDO:0003426.text: A benign neoplasm composed of glands containing epithelial clear cells.

MONDO:0003427.text: A benign lung neoplasm characterized by the presence of a fibrovascular stroma lined by cuboidal to columnar cells. Patients are usually asymptomatic and it is incidentally discovered as a pulmonary nodule during chest X-ray examination. Surgical excision is curative.

MONDO:0003428.text: A hemangioma arising from the brain.

MONDO:0003429.text: A hormone producing pituitary gland adenoma, associated with a hormonal syndrome.

MONDO:0003430.text: An adenoma or carcinoma of the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland that produces prolactin.

MONDO:0003431.text: An adenoma in which the neoplastic epithelial cells are admixed with adipose tissue cells.

MONDO:0003432.text: Strabismus is the intermittent or constant misalignment of an eye so that its line of vision is not pointed at the same object as the other eye. Strabismus is caused by an imbalance in the extraocular muscles which control the positioning of the eyes. Strabismus is normal in newborns but should resolve by the time the baby is 6 months old. In older children with strabismus, the brain may learn to ignore the input from one eye, and this may lead to amblyopia, a potentially permanent decrease in vision in that eye if not corrected.

MONDO:0003433.text: A rare parathyroid gland adenoma composed of neoplastic cells with abundant cytoplasm. The cytoplasm of the neoplastic cells is usually not entirely clear, and is often variably vacuolated, foamy, and granular.

MONDO:0003434.text: A glandular epithelial neoplasm that arises from the vagina and shows intestinal differentiation.

MONDO:0003435.text: A benign epithelial neoplasm characterized by a microcystic pattern. The cystic spaces are lined by small cuboidal cells without evidence of significant cytologic atypia.

MONDO:0003437.text: A small cell lung carcinoma detectable by sputum cytology only. The primary tumor is undetectable radiographically or during bronchoscopy; therefore, it can not be assessed.

MONDO:0003438.text: A morphologic variant of small cell lung carcinoma in combination with a non-small cell carcinoma.

MONDO:0003439.text: An exophytic glandular neoplasm of the bladder, morphologically similar to its intestinal counterpart. It often coexists with in situ or infiltrating bladder adenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0003441.text: A movement disorder characterized by sustained or intermittent muscle contractions, resulting in abnormal movements and/or postures.

MONDO:0003442.text: A papillary epithelial neoplasm that involves the urinary bladder urothelium.

MONDO:0003443.text: A neoplastic lesion of the urinary tract transitional cell epithelium characterized by papillary formations. -- 2003

MONDO:0003444.text: A rare adenoma that arises from the intrahepatic biliary tree.

MONDO:0003445.text: An adenoma that arises from the extrahepatic bile ducts. It is classified as papillary, tubular, or tubulopapillary.

MONDO:0003446.text: A benign neoplasm arising from the sweat glands. It presents as a slow growing cystic nodular lesion most often in the skin of the vulva and the perianal region. It is characterized by the presence of cystic and large papillary structures. The papillary structures contain connective tissue and are covered by two layers of epithelium. Complete excision is curative.

MONDO:0003447.text: An uncommon benign neoplasm of the sweat glands characterized by the presence of clear cells.

MONDO:0003448.text: A benign epithelial neoplasm with eccrine or apocrine differentiation, arising from the sweat glands. It usually presents as a solitary, well circumscribed, firm nodule in the face and upper trunk. It is characterized by the presence of basaloid cells forming nodules in the dermis. Cases of carcinoma arising from long standing spiradenomas have been reported.

MONDO:0003450.text: A benign neoplasm arising from the sweat glands. It is characterized by the presence of eccrine ducts in the dermis containing intraluminal papillary projections.

MONDO:0003452.text: Pathological processes of the snail-like structure (cochlea) of the inner ear (labyrinth) which can involve its nervous tissue, blood vessels, or fluid (endolymph).

MONDO:0003454.text: A malignant neoplasm involving the conjunctiva.

MONDO:0003455.text: A non-invasive, papillary epithelial neoplasm that arises from the epithelium of the intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts.

MONDO:0003458.text: A usually polypoid, benign neoplasm that arises from the endometrial cavity. It is characterized by the presence of a mesenchymal core component and an epithelial component that forms a lining on the mesenchymal core.

MONDO:0003459.text: A benign, polypoid neoplasm that arises from the cervix. It is characterized by the presence of epithelial and mesenchymal elements.

MONDO:0003460.text: A benign neoplasm characterized by the presence of glandular structures which contain clear cells and a fibrotic stroma.

MONDO:0003461.text: A rare, benign, asymptomatic neoplasm that arises from the fallopian tube. The majority of cases are incidental findings during operation for an unrelated gynecologic disorder. The tumors are round and solitary and contain connective tissue and papillary or tubular structures lined by serous-type epithelium.

MONDO:0003462.text: A biphasic polypoid neoplasm characterized by the presence of papillary projections that are lined by epithelial cells and fibrotic stroma.

MONDO:0003463.text: A benign neoplasm of the ovary characterized by the presence of glandular structures with endometrial-type well-differentiated cells in a fibrotic stroma.

MONDO:0003464.text: A benign or borderline neoplasm that arises from the ovaries and the fallopian tubes. It is characterized by the presence of cystic glandular structures and fibrous tissue.

MONDO:0003466.text: A synovial sarcoma characterized by the presence of a spindle cell component only.

MONDO:0003467.text: A synovial sarcoma arising from the mediastinum.

MONDO:0003468.text: A synovial sarcoma characterized by the presence of both an epithelial and a spindle cell component.

MONDO:0003469.text: A synovial sarcoma characterized by the presence of an epithelial cell component only. The epithelial cells are arranged in glandular or papillary structures.

MONDO:0003470.text: An ependymoma which shows conspicuous cellularity without a significant increase in mitotic rate. (Adapted from WHO)

MONDO:0003471.text: A infectious disease involving Pediculus humanus capitis.

MONDO:0003472.text: A contagious infestation of parasitic insects found on the head (Pediculus humanus capitis), body (Pediculus humanus corporis), or pubic area (Pthirus pubis) that typically cause itching and rash.

MONDO:0003473.text: An ependymoma that arises from the spinal cord.

MONDO:0003474.text: A variant of ependymoma, often found in the spinal cord, with tumor cells arranged in fascicles of variable width and cell density. Ependymal rosettes are generally absent, so this lesion must be distinguished from astrocytic neoplasms, but its EM characteristics are ependymal. (Adapted from WHO.)

MONDO:0003475.text: A rare variant of ependymoma characterized by well formed papillae. Tumor cell processes abutting capillaries are usually GFAP-positive. Differential diagnoses include choroid plexus papilloma, papillary meningioma and metastatic papillary carcinoma. (Adapted from WHO)

MONDO:0003476.text: An ependymoma, often supratentorial in location, characterized by the presence of ependymal cells with a perinuclear halo.

MONDO:0003477.text: An ependymoma that arises from the brain stem.

MONDO:0003478.text: An ependymoma that arises from the central nervous system and occurs during childhood.

MONDO:0003479.text: A pneumonia that is an acute inflammation of the lungs induced by inhalation of metal fumes or toxic gasses and vapors. It is a sentinel health event (occupational) associated with exposure to ammonia (refrigeration, fertilizer, and oil refining industries), chlorine (alkali and bleach industries), nitrogen oxides (silo fillers, arc welders, and nitric acid industry), sulfur dioxide (paper, refrigeration, and oil refining industries), cadmium (processors and cadmium smelters), trimellitic anhydride (plastics and organic chemical synthesis), and vanadium pentoxide (boilermakers). The two types of pulmonary agents are central and peripheral. Central pulmonary agents, for example, ammonia, are water soluble irritants that injure the upper airways. Peripheral pulmonary agents, for example, phosgene, NOx, and PFIB, are slightly water soluble irritants that injure the alveolar-capillary membranes. Chlorine has both central and peripheral effects.

MONDO:0003480.text: A dysgerminoma (disease) that involves the pineal body.

MONDO:0003481.text: A malignant germ cell tumor arising from the ovary. Morphologically, it is identical to seminoma and consists of a monotonous population of germ cells with abundant pale cytoplasm and uniform nuclei. The stroma invariably contains chronic inflammatory cells, mostly T-lymphocytes. It responds to chemotherapy or radiotherapy and the prognosis relates to the tumor stage.

MONDO:0003482.text: A infectious disease involving the Pediculus humanus corporis.

MONDO:0003486.text: A squamous cell carcinoma characterized by the presence of cells with hyperchromatic nuclei, scant amount of cytoplasm, and peripheral nuclear palisading.

MONDO:0003487.text: A squamous cell carcinoma characterized by the formation of gland-like structures.

MONDO:0003490.text: A carcinoma with squamous differentiation arising from the ampulla of Vater. Signs and symptoms include jaundice, abdominal pain, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, and weight loss.

MONDO:0003492.text: A squamous cell carcinoma that involves the lacrimal gland.

MONDO:0003493.text: A rare primary thymic carcinoma, characterized by the presence of keratinizing or non-keratinizing malignant squamous cells. Approximately 10-20% of cases occur in combination with thymoma. The prognosis depends on the tumor stage and the degree of cellular differentiation.

MONDO:0003494.text: A usually high grade squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the ovary and is not associated with a germ cell tumor. The prognosis is poor.

MONDO:0003495.text: A squamous cell tumor that arises from the ovary and is not associated with a germ cell tumor.

MONDO:0003497.text: A squamous cell carcinoma that involves the renal pelvis.

MONDO:0003499.text: A squamous cell carcinoma of the skin with a prominent spindle cell component.

MONDO:0003500.text: A squamous cell carcinoma that involves the bile duct.

MONDO:0003501.text: A squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the skin of the external ear.

MONDO:0003502.text: A rare squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the ureter.

MONDO:0003503.text: A rare squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the fallopian tube.

MONDO:0003504.text: A neoplasm with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the anal canal. It includes well differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (low and intermediate grade) and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (high grade).

MONDO:0003506.text: A rare choriocarcinoma that arises from a pulmonary artery.

MONDO:0003507.text: A choriocarcinoma arising from the ovary. When it appears before puberty is of germ cell origin. In children and young adults signs and symptoms include precocious pseudopuberty and vaginal bleeding. Serum human chorionic gonadotropin is elevated. Germ cell derived ovarian choriocarcinoma should be differentiated from primary or metastatic gestational choriocarcinoma affecting the ovary. The prognosis of germ cell derived choriocarcinoma is less favorable and requires more aggressive chemotherapy treatment regimens compared to gestational choriocarcinoma.

MONDO:0003508.text: A malignant germ cell tumor arising from the testis. It represents the rarest of the testicular germ cell tumors. Histologically it is characterized by the presence of syncytiotrophoblasts and cytotrophoblasts.

MONDO:0003509.text: A choriocarcinoma (disease) that involves the pineal body.

MONDO:0003510.text: A malignant tumor predominantly affecting young men and often associated with cryptorchidism. Seminoma is the most frequently seen malignant testicular germ cell tumor, followed by embryonal carcinoma and yolk sac tumor.

MONDO:0003512.text: A benign or malignant soft tissue neoplasm of the mediastinum. Representative examples of benign mediastinal soft tissue neoplasms include chondroma, leiomyoma, lipoma, and rhabdomyoma. Representative examples of malignant mediastinal soft tissue neoplasms include angiosarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, liposarcoma, osteosarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, and synovial sarcoma.

MONDO:0003513.text: A mature or immature teratoma that arises from the stomach.

MONDO:0003515.text: A teratoma that arises from the fallopian tube. It is a rare tumor, often found incidentally.

MONDO:0003516.text: A teratoma that occurs in an adult.

MONDO:0003517.text: A teratoma which may be cystic; it is composed entirely of well differentiated, adult-type tissues, without evidence of fetal-type tissues.

MONDO:0003518.text: A teratoma that involves the mediastinum.

MONDO:0003522.text: Persistent delay or absence in orgasm not accounted for by a medical reason.

MONDO:0003523.text: A gastrin-producing neuroendocrine tumor. It is usually located in the pancreas but it is also found at other anatomic sites, including the stomach and small intestine.

MONDO:0003524.text: A well differentiated neuroendocrine tumor that arises from the stomach. It produces gastrin and it may be associated with Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

MONDO:0003525.text: A usually malignant gastrin-producing neuroendocrine tumor arising from the pancreas. It may or may not be associated with inappropriate secretion of gastrin and an associated clinical syndrome.

MONDO:0003528.text: An ischemic contracture of the forearm that most often occurs secondary to trauma.

MONDO:0003532.text: A breast carcinoma characterized by the formation of irregular, finger-like projections of fibrous stroma covered with neoplastic epithelial cells.

MONDO:0003534.text: A rare primary thymic adenocarcinoma, characterized by a papillary growth pattern. There are only a few published cases, and no good data regarding prognosis.

MONDO:0003535.text: An adenocarcinoma that arises from the fallopian tube and is characterized by a papillary architectural pattern.

MONDO:0003537.text: A neoplasm of lymphoblasts committed to the T-cell lineage, typically composed of small to medium-sized blast cells. When the neoplasm involves predominantly the bone marrow and the peripheral blood, it is called T acute lymphoblastic leukemia. When it involves nodal or extranodal sites it is called T lymphoblastic lymphoma. (WHO, 2001)

MONDO:0003538.text: A neoplasm of immature malignant lymphocytes (lymphoblasts) committed to the B-cell or T-cell lineage. Neoplasms involving the bone marrow and the peripheral blood are called precursor lymphoblastic leukemias or acute lymphoblastic leukemias. Neoplasms involving primarily lymph nodes or extranodal sites are called lymphoblastic lymphomas. -- 2003

MONDO:0003539.text: An acute T-lymphoblastic leukemia occurring in adults.

MONDO:0003541.text: An acute lymphoblastic leukemia occurring during adulthood.

MONDO:0003543.text: A disease involving the trigeminal nerve.

MONDO:0003544.text: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm affecting the spinal cord. Representative examples include lymphoma, melanoma, and sarcoma.

MONDO:0003545.text: A neoplasm that occurs within the spinal canal in the space between the spinal cord and the dura mater. Representative examples include meningioma, neurofibroma, and sarcoma. Signs and symptoms include local and radicular pain, weakness and spinal cord compression.

MONDO:0003546.text: A disease involving the oculomotor nerve.

MONDO:0003548.text: An invasive breast carcinoma characterized by the presence of tubular and glandular neoplastic cell structures, admixed with islands of neoplastic cells showing squamous differentiation.

MONDO:0003549.text: An adenosquamous carcinoma that arises from the bile ducts.

MONDO:0003550.text: An esophageal carcinoma characterized by the presence of distinguishable squamous and glandular carcinomatous components.

MONDO:0003551.text: A rare carcinoma that arises from the thymus and is characterized by the presence of glandular and squamous carcinomatous components.

MONDO:0003553.text: A carcinoma with glandular and squamous differentiation arising from the ampulla of Vater. Signs and symptoms include jaundice, abdominal pain, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, and weight loss.

MONDO:0003554.text: An unusual colon carcinoma characterized by the presence of glandular and squamous carcinomatous components. The two carcinomatous components may be admixed within the tumor, or the two may appear separately in different areas.

MONDO:0003555.text: A carcinoma that arises from the Bartholin gland and is characterized by the presence of malignant glandular epithelial cells and malignant squamous epithelial cells.

MONDO:0003556.text: A rare endometrial carcinoma characterized by the presence of both malignant glandular and malignant squamous cellular components.

MONDO:0003557.text: A meningioma that affects the sheath of the optic nerve.

MONDO:0003558.text: An infrequent invasive carcinoma of the prostate gland characterized by the presence of both glandular and squamous neoplastic components. It is more often located in the transitional zone of the prostate gland and it tends to rapidly metastasize to the bones.

MONDO:0003561.text: An undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma characterized by the presence of osteoclast-like giant cells and cellular pleomorphism.

MONDO:0003562.text: A benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the rete testis. Representative examples include adenoma and adenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0003563.text: Diffuse replacement of the lung tissue by connective tissue.

MONDO:0003564.text: Replacement of the lung tissue by connective tissue in a specific area of the lung.

MONDO:0003565.text: An epithelial neoplasm of the urethra, which is morphologically characterized by the presence of a villous architectural pattern.

MONDO:0003568.text: A disease that involves the optic chiasma.

MONDO:0003569.text: A neoplastic or non-neoplastic disorder that affects one of the cranial nerves.

MONDO:0003570.text: A carcinoma characterized by the presence of malignant epithelial cells with clear cytoplasm which contains neutral lipids. A representative example is the lipid-rich breast carcinoma.

MONDO:0003572.text: A nonkeratinizing carcinoma which occurs predominantly in the nasopharynx but also in the tonsils and rarely in other anatomic sites. It is characterized by the presence of large malignant cells with vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, syncytial growth pattern, and a lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate.

MONDO:0003573.text: A usually aggressive malignant epithelial neoplasm composed of cells with significant cytologic atypia and nuclear pleomorphism.

MONDO:0003574.text: A malignant neoplasm involving the external ear.

MONDO:0003575.text: A high grade carcinoma characterized by the presence of comedo-type of tumor cell necrosis in which the necrotic areas are surrounded by a solid proliferation of malignant pleomorphic cells.

MONDO:0003578.text: A malignant non-seminomatous germ cell tumor that develops as a primary tumor in an anatomic site other than the testis or ovary.

MONDO:0003579.text: A disease that involves the nerve fiber layer of retina.

MONDO:0003581.text: An embryonal carcinoma arising from the ovary. Signs and symptoms include the presence of an abdominal mass and abdominal pain.

MONDO:0003582.text: An autosomal dominant inherited syndrome caused by mutations in the BRCA1 or BRCA2 genes. Patients are at high risk of developing breast cancer, particularly before the age of fifty, high risk of developing a second primary breast cancer, and high risk of developing both breast and ovarian cancer.

MONDO:0003584.text: A disease involving the visual cortex.

MONDO:0003585.text: A malignant neoplasm arising from adipocytes, that occurs in adults. The tumor maybe one of several histologic types including well-differentiated, dedifferentiated, myxoid/round cell, and pleomorphic liposarcoma.

MONDO:0003586.text: A malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the esophagus, characterized by multivacuolated lipoblasts with hyperchromatic nuclei, a solid pattern of growth, and a rich vascular network. It arises from the mucosal and submucosal layers of the lower esophagus. Clinical presentation includes progressive dysphagia, nausea, throat discomfort, and foreign body sensation.

MONDO:0003587.text: A rare malignant neoplasm arising from adipocytes, that occurs in children. The tumor maybe one of several histologic types including well-differentiated, dedifferentiated, myxoid/round cell, and pleomorphic liposarcoma.

MONDO:0003588.text: A rare malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the larynx. It predominantly affects males. Clinical presentation includes dysphonia, dysphagia and respiratory symptoms. The supraglottis is the most common site of involvement.

MONDO:0003589.text: A malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the ovary.

MONDO:0003590.text: A liposarcoma characterized by the presence of a fibroblastic component.

MONDO:0003591.text: A rare malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the fat cells surrounding the kidney, usually of the well-differentiated or myxoid type. It may be associated with tuberous sclerosis.

MONDO:0003592.text: A malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the stomach.

MONDO:0003593.text: A malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the breast.

MONDO:0003594.text: A malignant neoplasm characterized by the presence of a combination of liposarcomatous morphologic subtypes: myxoid/round cell and well differentiated/dedifferentiated liposarcoma or myxoid/round cell and pleomorphic liposarcoma.

MONDO:0003595.text: A morphologic variant of well differentiated liposarcoma occurring most often in the retroperitoneum and paratesticular area. It is characterized by the presence of bizarre hyperchromatic stromal cells and rare multivacuolated lipoblasts within a fibrous stroma.

MONDO:0003596.text: A morphologic variant of well differentiated liposarcoma characterized by the presence of bland spindle cells and lipoblasts within a myxoid or fibrous stroma.

MONDO:0003598.text: Disease involving the median nerve, from its origin at the brachial plexus to its termination in the hand. Clinical features include weakness of wrist and finger flexion, forearm pronation, thenar abduction, and loss of sensation over the lateral palm, first three fingers, and radial half of the ring finger. Common sites of injury include the elbow, where the nerve passes through the two heads of the pronator teres muscle (pronator syndrome) and in the carpal tunnel (carpal tunnel syndrome).

MONDO:0003599.text: A rare malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the vulva.

MONDO:0003600.text: A malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the skin.

MONDO:0003601.text: A malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the anterior, middle or posterior mediastinum.

MONDO:0003602.text: A malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the intracranial region.

MONDO:0003603.text: A hormone producing or non-producing pituitary gland adenoma or carcinoma, not associated with a hormonal syndrome.

MONDO:0003604.text: A hormone producing pituitary gland tumor, associated with a hormonal syndrome.

MONDO:0003606.text: A malignant neoplasm involving the adrenal medulla

MONDO:0003607.text: A neuritis that involves the forelimb.

MONDO:0003608.text: A disorder characterized by loss of optic nerve fibers. It may be inherited or acquired. Acquired causes include ischemia, optic nerve neuropathy, glaucoma, trauma, radiation, brain tumors, and multiple sclerosis. It leads to vision disturbances.

MONDO:0003609.text: A rare benign cystadenoma that arises from the seminal vesicle.

MONDO:0003610.text: An exceptionally rare cystadenoma that arises from the rete ovarii.

MONDO:0003611.text: A benign mesonephric neoplasm that arises from the uterine ligament and occurs in women with von Hippel-Lindau disease. It is a cystic lesion characterized by the presence of multiple papillary excrescences.

MONDO:0003612.text: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the uterine ligament.

MONDO:0003614.text: A rare benign neoplasm characterized by the presence of smooth muscle cells growing within veins.

MONDO:0003615.text: Any nerve disorder caused by the entrapment and compression of a nerve.

MONDO:0003616.text: Formation of nodules in the isthmus of the fallopian tube due to fallopian tube diverticulosis. It may cause infertility or ectopic pregnancy.

MONDO:0003617.text: Chronic inflammation of the fallopian tube. It usually follows an acute inflammatory attack.

MONDO:0003618.text: The presence of pus in the fallopian tube. It is usually caused by acute salpingitis. The fallopian tube is distended and filled with pus. Histologic examination reveals edema and acute and chronic inflammation. Symptoms include fever, vaginal discharge, and pelvic pain.

MONDO:0003619.text: Acute or chronic inflammation of the fallopian tube. It is most often caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis infections. The infections usually originate in the vagina and ascend to the fallopian tube. Symptoms include abdominal, pelvic, and lower back pain, pain during ovulation and sexual intercourse, fever, nausea, and vomiting. Complications include infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

MONDO:0003620.text: A disease involving the peripheral nervous system.

MONDO:0003621.text: A neuroendocrine tumor that arises from the small intestine and produces vasoactive intestinal peptide.

MONDO:0003622.text: A usually malignant pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor producing vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP). It may or may not be associated with inappropriate secretion of VIP and an associated clinical syndrome.

MONDO:0003624.text: A breast adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of serous (acinic cell) differentiation.

MONDO:0003626.text: A rare serous adenocarcinoma that arises from the uterine ligament.

MONDO:0003627.text: A rheumatologic disorder that involves the pulmonary valve.

MONDO:0003628.text: A disease involving the pulmonary valve.

MONDO:0003630.text: A metastasizing, slow-growing malignant epithelial neoplasm that arises from the exocrine pancreas. It is characterized by the presence of cysts and is composed of glycogen-rich malignant epithelial cells which produce a watery fluid. Signs and symptoms include upper gastrointestinal bleeding, weight loss, jaundice, and abdominal pain.

MONDO:0003631.text: A rare adenocarcinoma that arises from the cervix. It is characterized by the presence of papillary patterns and cellular budding. Psammoma bodies are often seen.

MONDO:0003633.text: A term describing a malignant soft tissue tumor which consists of two or more mesenchymal lines of differentiation, excluding a fibroblastic line of differentiation.

MONDO:0003634.text: The presence of abnormal amounts of protein in the urine.

MONDO:0003635.text: A very rare breast adenocarcinoma with sebaceous differentiation.

MONDO:0003636.text: A carcinoma that arises from the vulva. It is characterized by the presence of malignant basaloid glandular epithelial cells that resemble sebaceous epithelium and are arranged in cords and nests.

MONDO:0003637.text: A rare benign lung tumor with perivascular epithelioid cell differentiation. It is composed of round or oval cells with abundant clear or eosinophilic cytoplasm and distinct cell borders. The vast majority of patients are asymptomatic and the tumors are discovered incidentally. Excision is curative.

MONDO:0003638.text: A primary or metastatic meningioma that is present in the lung. The lung is the most frequent site of metastasis of meningiomas.

MONDO:0003639.text: A benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from the hilar region of the lung.

MONDO:0003640.text: A rare, benign wart-like skin lesion of unknown etiology that is usually found in the genital or perianal area and consists of hyperkeratosis and aggregates of foam cell macrophages.

MONDO:0003641.text: A primary or metastatic neoplasm of hematopoietic origin that affects the brain, meninges, or spinal cord. Representative examples include Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas, histiocytic tumors, and leukemias.

MONDO:0003643.text: A cavernous hemangioma characterized by the presence of hylanized vascular channels and is often associated with the presence of calcifications, fibrosis, and hemorrhage.

MONDO:0003644.text: A cavernous hemangioma arising from the colon.

MONDO:0003645.text: A cavernous hemangioma arising from the face.

MONDO:0003646.text: A neoplasm with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the rectum. It includes well differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (low and intermediate grade) and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (high grade).

MONDO:0003648.text: A disease involving the tympanic membrane.

MONDO:0003649.text: A well differentiated, low or intermediate grade tumor with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the esophagus.

MONDO:0003650.text: A hepatoblastoma characterized by the presence of fetal and embryonal epithelial components and a mesenchymal component.

MONDO:0003651.text: A pure fetal or fetal and embryonal epithelial hepatoblastoma characterized by the presence of broad trabeculae.

MONDO:0003652.text: Urolithiasis in which the composition of the stones is predominantly urate.

MONDO:0003654.text: A low grade malignant bone-forming mesenchymal neoplasm arising from the surface of the bone. It occurs in childhood and usually affects the distal posterior femur, the proximal tibia, and proximal humerus. Painless swelling is the usual clinical sign. The prognosis is usually excellent.

MONDO:0003655.text: A non-Hodgkin or Hodgkin lymphoma that arises in the cerebral hemispheres as a primary lesion.

MONDO:0003656.text: A laboratory test result which indicates free hemoglobin in the urine.

MONDO:0003658.text: A group of lymphomas displaying molecular, morphologic, immunophenotypic, and clinical overlap between classical Hodgkin lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. This term particularly applies to mediastinal lymphomas with overlapping features of mediastinal (thymic) large B-cell lymphoma and classical Hodgkin lymphoma.

MONDO:0003659.text: A Hodgkin or non-Hodgkin lymphoma that occurs during childhood.

MONDO:0003660.text: A lymphoma that occurs in an adult.

MONDO:0003661.text: A lymphoma that arises from the breast. There is no history of extramammary breast lymphoma and ipsilateral axillary lymph node involvement does not exclude the diagnosis of primary breast lymphoma. Most patients present with a painless breast lump. The vast majority of cases are B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, follicular lymphoma, and extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of mucosa associated lymphoid tissue are the most common types of primary non-Hodgkin lymphoma of the breast. Primary Hodgkin lymphoma of the breast is rare.

MONDO:0003663.text: A rare endometrioid adenocarcinoma that arises from the uterine ligament. Some of the reported cases were associated with endometriosis.

MONDO:0003664.text: Anemia resulting from the premature destruction of the peripheral blood red cells. It may be congenital or it may be caused by infections, medications, or malignancies.

MONDO:0003665.text: A cervical adenocarcinoma with the histologic characteristics of the endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium.

MONDO:0003666.text: An adenocarcinoma that arises from the fallopian tube and resembles the endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the uterus. It usually has a favorable prognosis.

MONDO:0003669.text: A malignant germ cell tumor arising from the testis. It is believed that it is derived from the sexually undifferentiated embryonic gonad. Treatment with radiotherapy is highly successful when the tumor is diagnosed in localized stages, which represents the majority of presentations of seminoma.

MONDO:0003670.text: An electrocardiographic finding of an injury in leads corresponding to the anatomic region of the posteroinferior wall of the heart.

MONDO:0003671.text: A myocardial infarction (disease) that involves the cardiac septum.

MONDO:0003673.text: An electrocardiographic finding of an injury in leads corresponding to the anatomic region of the apex of the heart.

MONDO:0003674.text: An electrocardiographic finding of an injury in leads corresponding to the anatomic region of the subendocardial layer of the wall of the heart.

MONDO:0003675.text: An electrocardiographic finding of an injury in leads corresponding to the anatomic region of the posterolateral wall of the heart.

MONDO:0003676.text: An electrocardiographic finding of an injury in leads corresponding to the anatomic region of the inferolateral wall of the heart.

MONDO:0003678.text: A history of myocardial infarction in the absence of clinical symptoms and positive electrocardiographic findings.

MONDO:0003680.text: A chondrosarcoma arising from the surface of bone. It is characterized by a lobulated growth pattern, high mitotic activity, myxoid stroma formation, and necrotic changes. It occurs in adults. Clinical presentation includes pain, and sometimes swelling.

MONDO:0003681.text: A chondrosarcoma characterized by the presence of myxoid changes.

MONDO:0003682.text: A non-disseminated skeletal or extraskeletal chondrosarcoma.

MONDO:0003684.text: A rare, usually low grade chondrosarcoma characterized by the presence of tumor cells with clear cytoplasm. It usually arises in the epiphyseal ends of long bones.

MONDO:0003685.text: A germ cell tumor that involves the retroperitoneal space.

MONDO:0003686.text: A benign or malignant sweat gland neoplasm with apocrine differentiation. Representative examples include apocrine adenoma, ceruminous adenocarcinoma, and apocrine breast carcinoma.

MONDO:0003687.text: A malignant neoplasm involving the endocardium.

MONDO:0003688.text: A localized or multifocal mesothelioma arising from the peritoneum and less often the pleura. Cases arising from the peritoneum predominantly occur in women. It is characterized by the formation of papillae, covered by a single layer of blunt mesothelial cells. Mitotic figures are not present. There is no evidence of severe cytologic atypia. It has a relatively favorable clinical outcome, compared to malignant mesothelioma.

MONDO:0003689.text: A congenital hemolytic anemia caused by defects of the erythrocyte membrane, enzyme deficiencies, or hemoglobinopathies.

MONDO:0003690.text: An anaplastic ependymoma occurring in adults.

MONDO:0003691.text: A malignant mesenchymoma occurring in children.

MONDO:0003692.text: A malignant mesenchymoma occurring in adults.

MONDO:0003693.text: A benign neoplasm characterized by the presence of cystic glandular and fibrous tissues and clear cells.

MONDO:0003694.text: A benign neoplasm of glandular epithelium characterized by the presence of clear or hobnail cells within a dense fibrous stroma and cystic structures.

MONDO:0003695.text: An uncommon benign neoplasm of glandular epithelium characterized by the presence of clear or hobnail cells within a dense fibrous stroma.

MONDO:0003698.text: A slow growing, locally recurring, very well differentiated papillary squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the penis. It is characterized by the presence of acanthosis and hyperkeratosis. The neoplastic infiltrate extends into the underlying stroma with a pushing border. Koilocytotic atypia is not present.

MONDO:0003699.text: An anxiety disorder characterized by an intense, irrational fear of an object, activity, or situation. The individual seeks to avoid the object, activity, or situation. In adults, the individual recognizes that the fear is excessive or unreasonable.

MONDO:0003700.text: A neoplasm (disease) that involves the brachial nerve plexus.

MONDO:0003701.text: A morphologic variant of papillary carcinoma of the thyroid gland that more often affects young patients and commonly metastasizing to the lungs. It is characterized by a diffuse infiltration of the thyroid gland by malignant follicular cells, squamous metaplasia, stromal fibrosis, and lymphocytic infiltration.

MONDO:0003702.text: A rare benign neoplasm characterized by the presence of smooth muscle cells growing within the veins of the uterine corpus. The intravascular neoplasm growth occurs outside the confines of an adjacent leiomyoma.

MONDO:0003704.text: An unusual condition characterized by the presence of numerous small benign smooth muscle neoplasms located throughout the body of the uterus.

MONDO:0003707.text: A carcinoma that arises from the common bile duct distal to the insertion of the cystic duct.

MONDO:0003708.text: An aggressive, high-grade and poorly differentiated carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the extrahepatic bile ducts. It is characterized by the presence of malignant small cells.

MONDO:0003709.text: An anxiety disorder characterized by an intense, irrational fear of venturing out into open places or situations in which help (or escape) might not be available should excessive anxiety or panic symptoms develop.

MONDO:0003710.text: An ovarian malignant germ cell tumor characterized by the presence of at least two different germ cell components. At least one of the germ cell components is primitive. The most common combination of germ cell elements is dysgerminoma and yolk sac tumor.

MONDO:0003715.text: Urachal cancer is a type of bladder cancer, making up less than 1% of all bladder cancers. The urachus is a structure normally only present during development in the womb that connects the bellybutton and the bladder. This connection normally disappears before birth, but in some people remains. Urachalcancers are usually diagnosed in adults in their 50's and 60's and may develop at the dome or anterior wall of the bladder, along the midline of the body (including the belly button), and between the pubis symphasis and the bladder.Most urachal cancersare adenocarcinomas (cancers that develop from gland cells).Others may besarcomas (which develop from connective tissue -such as leiomyosarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, and malignant fibrous histiocytoma), small cell carcinomas, transitional cell cancer, and mixed neoplasias. Most individuals with urachal cancer have symptoms of with hematuria (blood in urine). Other symptoms may include abdominal pain, a palpable abdominal mass, mucinuria, and bacteriuria. Treatment usually involved surgery to remove the cancer.

MONDO:0003716.text: A papillary transitional cell carcinoma that arises from the renal pelvis.

MONDO:0003717.text: A papillary tumor originating in the renal pelvis.

MONDO:0003719.text: A neoplasm (disease) that involves the renal pelvis.

MONDO:0003720.text: A usually aggressive malignant neoplasm arising from the kidney. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and collagenous stroma formation in a herringbone growth pattern.

MONDO:0003721.text: An osteosarcoma arising from the kidney.

MONDO:0003722.text: A meningioma that affects the internal auditory canal.

MONDO:0003724.text: Breast fibrocystic change characterized by the absence of epithelial cell hyperplasia.

MONDO:0003725.text: A non-neoplastic disorder characterized by epithelial and/or myoepithelial tissue growth in the breast lobules. It may be associated with apocrine changes or sclerosis.

MONDO:0003726.text: Breast adenosis characterized by the presence of extensive apocrine metaplasia.

MONDO:0003727.text: An overwhelming, irrational, and persistent fear of animals.

MONDO:0003728.text: A usually aggressive malignant neoplasm arising from the breast. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and collagenous stroma formation in a herringbone growth pattern.

MONDO:0003729.text: Infiltration of the skin and subcutaneous tissue by leukemic cells without evidence of leukemia in the bone marrow and peripheral blood. It results in clinically identifiable skin lesions. It may be the first manifestation of acute leukemia, preceding the involvement of the bone marrow and peripheral blood by the leukemic process.

MONDO:0003730.text: A leukemia characterized by the absence of leukemic cells in the peripheral blood.

MONDO:0003731.text: A mature or immature teratoma affecting the central nervous system and occurring in adults.

MONDO:0003732.text: A central nervous system mature teratoma that occurs in an adult.

MONDO:0003733.text: A teratoma composed exclusively of fully differentiated, 'adult-type' tissue elements that are sometimes arranged in a pattern resembling normal tissue relationships. Mitotic activity is low or absent. The more common ectodermal components present in a mature teratoma include skin, brain and choroid plexus. The more common mesodermal components include cartilage, bone, fat and muscle (both smooth and striated). And the most common endodermal components are cysts lined by epithelia of respiratory or enteric type and in some cases pancreatic or hepatic tissue. (Adapted from WHO)

MONDO:0003735.text: A variant of teratoma composed of incompletely differentiated components resembling fetal tissues. Even if the immature component is only a minor element of an otherwise differentiated teratoma, the tumor is still classified as immature. (Adapted from WHO)

MONDO:0003736.text: An overwhelming, irrational, and persistent fear of being diagnosed with cancer.

MONDO:0003737.text: A Leydig cell tumor characterized by a large size, cellular atypia, high mitotic activity, vascular invasion and necrotic changes. The prognosis is usually poor.

MONDO:0003738.text: A rare dysgammaglobulinemia characterized by low or undetectable serum levels of immunoglobulin class E (IgE). It is an uncommon primary antibody deficiency. It is most likely an inherited immunodeficiency. It may be caused by decreased or inefficient class-switching from progenitor B cells without any corresponding decreases in the other isotypes. Most affected persons appear asymptomatic but may show a predisposition to autoimmune and respiratory diseases.

MONDO:0003739.text: A broad classification of dysgammaglobulinemias characterized by low or undetectable serum levels of one of the five immunoglobulin classes. Deficiencies of immunoglobulins present variably according to isotype. Selective deficiencies may be caused by decreased or inefficient production from progenitor B cells without any corresponding decreases in the other isotypes. The clinical course and prognosis is dependent upon the severity of the selective deficiency and associated morbidity.

MONDO:0003740.text: An overwhelming, irrational, and persistent fear of contracting Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.

MONDO:0003741.text: A rare sex cord-stromal tumor that arises from the testis. It is the most frequent congenital testicular neoplasm and is usually diagnosed during the perinatal period. It usually presents as an asymptomatic scrotal or abdominal mass. Morphologically it is characterized by the presence of cysts that are lined by cells resembling granulosa and theca cells.

MONDO:0003742.text: A usually aggressive malignant neoplasm arising from the heart. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and collagenous stroma formation in a herringbone growth pattern.

MONDO:0003743.text: A malignant hemangiopericytoma arising in the heart.

MONDO:0003744.text: A melanoma arising from the choroid, ciliary body, or the iris. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped melanocytes.

MONDO:0003745.text: A spindle cell melanoma that involves the optic choroid.

MONDO:0003746.text: A spindle cell melanoma that involves the ciliary body.

MONDO:0003747.text: A glomus tumor characterized by huge vascular channel formations.

MONDO:0003748.text: An overwhelming, irrational, and persistent fear of traveling in an aircraft.

MONDO:0003749.text: A non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the esophagus. Representative examples of non-neoplastic disorders include esophagitis and esophageal ulcer. Representative examples of neoplastic disorders include carcinomas, lymphomas, and melanomas.

MONDO:0003750.text: A germ cell tumor of the central nervous system occurring in children.

MONDO:0003751.text: A germ cell tumor that occurs during childhood.

MONDO:0003752.text: A papilloma that arises from the ciliated respiratory mucosa that lines the frontal sinus. It is classified as inverted papilloma and oncocytic papilloma.

MONDO:0003753.text: A benign exophytic squamous cell neoplasm with papillary growth that arises from the nasal vestibule.

MONDO:0003754.text: Brown-Sequard syndrome is a rare neurological condition that results from an injury or damage to one side of the spinal cord. This condition results in weakness or paralysis on one side of the body (hemiparaplegia) and a loss of sensation on the opposite side (hemianesthesia). Brown-Sequard syndrome most commonly occurs in the the thoracic spine (upper and middle back). There are several causes of Brown-Sequard syndrome, including: a spinal cord tumor, trauma (such as a puncture wound to the neck or back), infectious or inflammatory diseases (tuberculosis or multiple sclerosis), and disk herniation. Treatment for this condition varies depending on the underlying cause.

MONDO:0003756.text: A benign, borderline, or malignant epithelial tumor of the ovary characterized by the presence of neoplastic epithelial cells that contain intracytoplasmic mucin and may resemble the epithelial cells of the endocervix or gastrointestinal tract.

MONDO:0003757.text: Complete paralysis of the lower half of the body including both legs, often caused by damage to the spinal cord.

MONDO:0003758.text: A germ cell tumor that arises from the testis during childhood.

MONDO:0003759.text: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the ovary and occurs in children.

MONDO:0003760.text: A germ cell tumor that arises from the ovary and occurs in children.

MONDO:0003761.text: A melanoma that arises from leptomeningeal melanocytes.

MONDO:0003762.text: A primary or metastatic malignant tumor involving the leptomeninges.

MONDO:0003763.text: An anxiety disorder precipitated by an experience of intense fear or horror while exposed to a traumatic (especially life-threatening) event. The disorder is characterized by dissociative symptoms; vivid recollections of the traumatic event; avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event; and a constant state of hyperarousal for no more than one month.

MONDO:0003764.text: A melanoma that arises from leptomeningeal melanocytes and occurs in childhood.

MONDO:0003765.text: A melanoma that arises from leptomeningeal melanocytes and occurs in adulthood.

MONDO:0003766.text: A cancer involving a dorsal plus ventral thalamus.

MONDO:0003767.text: A disease involving the mitral valve.

MONDO:0003768.text: A rare cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of signet ring cells.

MONDO:0003770.text: A meningioma that arises from the meninges of the thoracic region of the spinal cord.

MONDO:0003771.text: A meningioma that affects the jugular foramen.

MONDO:0003772.text: A meningioma that affects the cerebral hemispheres.

MONDO:0003773.text: A cystic meningioma that grows within the cerebral hemispheres.

MONDO:0003774.text: A meningioma that affects the cerebral sulcus.

MONDO:0003775.text: A meningioma that affects the lateral ventricle of the brain.

MONDO:0003776.text: A neoplasm of the renal pelvis in which the epithelial cells grow downward into the underlying supportive tissue.

MONDO:0003777.text: A benign neoplasm of the renal pelvis that involves the transitional epithelium projecting above the surrounding epithelial surface and consisting of villous or arborescent outgrowths of fibrovascular stroma.

MONDO:0003778.text: A disorder in which the immune system is unable to mount an adequate immune response.

MONDO:0003780.text: A broad classification of disorders that affect the cell-mediated aspect of the immune response. Circulating numbers of T lymphocytes are decreased or ineffective.

MONDO:0003781.text: An acute or chronic inflammatory process affecting the bronchi.

MONDO:0003782.text: A morphologic variant of leiomyosarcoma arising from the uterine corpus. It is characterized by the presence of epithelioid round cells with eosinophilic to clear cytoplasm.

MONDO:0003783.text: Reduction in the number of lymphocytes.

MONDO:0003784.text: A in situ carcinoma that involves the nasal cavity.

MONDO:0003785.text: A laboratory test result indicating a decreased number of white blood cells in the peripheral blood.

MONDO:0003786.text: A choriocarcinoma that arises from the testis during childhood.

MONDO:0003787.text: A malignant mixed germ cell neoplasm that arises from the testis during childhood.

MONDO:0003788.text: An embryonal carcinoma that arises from the testis during childhood.

MONDO:0003789.text: A familial carcinoma inherited in an autosomal dominant trait. It is characterized by the development of multiple, bilateral papillary renal cell carcinomas. The carcinomas range from microscopic lesions to clinically symptomatic tumors. It is associated with activating mutations of the MET oncogene.

MONDO:0003790.text: An urothelial carcinoma that arises from the urothelial lining of the prostatic urethra.

MONDO:0003791.text: A male urethral cancer that involves the prostatic urethra.

MONDO:0003792.text: A highly aggressive malignant neoplasm arising from the ovary. Morphologically, it is a high grade tumor, composed of carcinomatous and sarcomatous elements.

MONDO:0003795.text: A carcinoma that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of small malignant cells. It includes small cell carcinoma, hypercalcemic type and small cell carcinoma, pulmonary type.

MONDO:0003796.text: A Kaposi sarcoma arising from the rectum.

MONDO:0003799.text: Inflammation of the conjunctiva of the eye.

MONDO:0003800.text: A malignant hemangiopericytoma characterized by the presence of necrotic changes and in some cases high mitotic activity.

MONDO:0003801.text: A squamous cell intraepithelial neoplasia that involves the cornea.

MONDO:0003802.text: A malignant neoplasm involving the cornea.

MONDO:0003803.text: A disease involving the aortic valve.

MONDO:0003805.text: A rare neoplasm of mesothelial origin that arises from the pericardium.

MONDO:0003806.text: A rare, circumscribed or encapsulated tumor arising from the follicular cells of the thyroid gland. It is characterized by a trabecular growth pattern and hyalinized stroma formation. The vast majority of cases have a benign clinical course.

MONDO:0003808.text: An osteosarcoma arising from the mediastinum.

MONDO:0003809.text: A malignant hemangiopericytoma arising in the mediastinum.

MONDO:0003810.text: A rare morphologic variant of bladder adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of malignant glandular epithelial cells and clear cells forming a diffuse pattern.

MONDO:0003811.text: A benign, borderline, or malignant mixed epithelial tumor of the ovary. It is characterized by the presence of more than one epithelial cell type, most often serous and endocervical-type mucinous.

MONDO:0003812.text: A benign, borderline, or malignant epithelial tumor of the ovary characterized by the presence of glands and/or cysts lined by neoplastic cells that resemble endometrial cells.

MONDO:0003813.text: A benign, borderline, or malignant epithelial tumor that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of papillary proliferations. Representative examples include surface papilloma, borderline serous surface papillary tumor, and serous surface papillary adenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0003816.text: A disease involving the articular cartilage of joint.

MONDO:0003818.text: A mature teratoma that arises from the ovary and occurs in children.

MONDO:0003819.text: A mature or immature teratoma that arises from the ovary and occurs in children.

MONDO:0003820.text: An ovarian teratoma which may be cystic, composed entirely of well differentiated, adult-type tissues, without evidence of fetal-type tissues.

MONDO:0003821.text: A germ cell tumor that arises from the ovary and is composed of tissues that originate from two or three of the following germ layers, endoderm, ectoderm, or mesoderm.

MONDO:0003822.text: A papillary neoplasm of the urinary bladder in which the transitional cells form papillae. The papillary structures exhibit minimal architectural distortion and minimal atypia. Mitoses are infrequent. Patients are at an increased risk of developing new papillary lesions. Occasionally, the new lesions are urothelial carcinomas.

MONDO:0003824.text: An inherited condition characterized by the development of kidney oncocytomas which are often bilateral and multifocal. This condition may be connected to Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome.

MONDO:0003825.text: A benign tumor of the kidney, characterized by the presence of large cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm. The majority of these tumors are discovered incidentally, during work-up of other conditions.

MONDO:0003826.text: An extragonadal malignant germ cell tumor that arises from the mediastinum. It is characterized by the presence of uniform cells with clear or eosinophilic cytoplasm, round nucleus with one or more nucleoli, and distinct cellular borders. It usually arises from the anterior mediastinum. It may present with respiratory distress, chest pain, or superior vena cava syndrome or it may be asymptomatic, with the tumor detected on routine chest x-ray. The prognosis of mediastinal pure seminomas is favorable compared to the mediastinal non-seminomatous malignant germ cell tumors.

MONDO:0003827.text: A broad classification for humoral immunodeficiencies. These disorders may be caused by inadequate activation of progenitor B cells, defective class-switching or the effects of medications. Despite the potential for increased susceptibility to infection, these disorders are self-limited with eventual normalization of serum antibody levels.

MONDO:0003828.text: A rare, hormonally functioning or non-functioning pituitary gland adenocarcinoma that produces growth hormone. It may be associated with acromegaly.

MONDO:0003829.text: A controversial term, used for renal papillary lesions which measure 1cm or less in diameter and contain small, regular nuclei.

MONDO:0003832.text: A genetic deficiency of any of the component of the complement system (including the classical, alternative, and terminal pathway components), that can either be acquired or inherited.

MONDO:0003834.text: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the cardia of stomach.

MONDO:0003835.text: A carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the cardia of stomach.

MONDO:0003836.text: A rare, hormonally functioning or non-functioning pituitary gland adenocarcinoma that produces thyrotropin.

MONDO:0003837.text: An adenoma or carcinoma of the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland that produces thyrotropin.

MONDO:0003839.text: A malignant neoplasm of the ovary with an invasive epithelial component and a fibrotic stroma. The epithelial component is characterized by the presence of malignant epithelial cells with intracytoplasmic mucin. Cystic spaces are also present which contain mucoid material.

MONDO:0003840.text: A rare benign adipose tissue neoplasm of the epicardium of the heart.

MONDO:0003841.text: A rare benign adipose tissue neoplasm of the heart usually originating in the epicardial or pericardial fatty tissue.

MONDO:0003842.text: Benign and malignant astrocytomas that arise from astrocytes in the cerebellum. More than 80% of childhood cerebellar astrocytomas are pilocytic astrocytomas which have a favorable prognosis. The remainder are composed of diffuse or fibrillary subtypes with malignant astrocytomas occurring only rarely in the cerebellum during childhood.

MONDO:0003843.text: A rare benign adipose tissue neoplasm within the cerebral hemisphere often associated with partial or complete agenesis of the corpus callosum.

MONDO:0003844.text: A rare benign adipose tissue neoplasm of the central nervous system frequently found in midline locations such as the corpus callosum, the quadrigeminal plate, the hypothalamus, the spinal canal or the cauda equina. Some contain Schwann cells, bone, cartilage or hamartomatous blood vessels.

MONDO:0003845.text: A rare benign adipose tissue neoplasm of the corpus callosum.

MONDO:0003846.text: Viral infection of the esophagus. It often occurs in immunocompromised patients and it is caused by cytomegalovirus or herpes simplex virus. Symptoms include pain on swallowing, fever, and retrosternal burning.

MONDO:0003847.text: A disease that is caused by genetic modifications where those modifications are inherited from a parent's genome.

MONDO:0003848.text: A condition in which the thymus gland is abnomally located; this can be secondary to failure of descent during fetal development, or failure of involution.

MONDO:0003849.text: A slow-growing malignant bone tumor arising from the remnants of the notochord and occurring in the clivus. It is characterized by a lobulated growth pattern, myxoid stroma formation, and the presence of physaliphorous cells.

MONDO:0003850.text: A slow-growing malignant bone tumor arising from the remnants of the notochord and occurring in the clivus. It is characterized by a lobulated growth pattern, myxoid stroma formation, the presence of physaliphorous cells and cartilage.

MONDO:0003851.text: A rare type of teratoma that arises from the ovary and resembles a malformed fetus.

MONDO:0003852.text: A mature teratoma that arises from the ovary and presents as a large solid mass. It contains multiple cysts that vary in size. Small foci of hemorrhage are also present.

MONDO:0003853.text: A carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the major vestibular gland.

MONDO:0003856.text: A malignant hemangiopericytoma occurring in the adult population.

MONDO:0003857.text: A solitary fibrous tumor/hemangiopericytoma, grade 3 that arises from the brain and occurs in the adult population.

MONDO:0003858.text: A meningioma that affects the anterior visual pathway.

MONDO:0003859.text: Meningiomas that affects both optic nerves.

MONDO:0003860.text: A meningioma that affects the cerebellopontine angle.

MONDO:0003861.text: An eccrine adenocarcinoma that arises from the sweat glands in the vulva.

MONDO:0003862.text: A malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor characterized by the presence of malignant cells that contain melanin and formation of psammoma bodies.

MONDO:0003863.text: A rare variant of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor. It is characterized by the presence of malignant cells that contain melanin.

MONDO:0003864.text: An indolent, mature B-cell neoplasm composed of small, round B-lymphocytes. When the bone marrow and peripheral blood are involved, the term chronic lymphocytic leukemia is used. The term small lymphocytic lymphoma is restricted to cases which do not show leukemic involvement of the bone marrow and peripheral blood.

MONDO:0003865.text: A form of melanoma occurring most often on the plantar, palmar, subungual, and periungual skin. It presents as a pigmented macular lesion with irregular borders. Morphologically, it consists of atypical spindled and dendritic melanocytes. The epidermis is often hyperplastic and there is pagetoid infiltration of the epidermis by anaplastic cells.

MONDO:0003866.text: An osteosarcoma arising from the liver.

MONDO:0003867.text: A diffuse or multifocal proliferation of uniform nevoid polygonal cells in the leptomeninges. Cells may spread into the Virchow-Robin spaces without frank invasion of the brain. Diffuse melanocytosis carries a poor prognosis even in the absence of histologic malignancy. (WHO)

MONDO:0003868.text: A meningioma that affects the anterior foramen magnum.

MONDO:0003869.text: An abnormal growth of the cells that comprise the tissues of the brainstem. While the tumor may be histologically benign, it can produce great morbidity due to its location. It presents most commonly in the first two decades of life.

MONDO:0003870.text: An astrocytoma that arises from the brain stem and occurs during childhood.

MONDO:0003872.text: A serous cystadenoma of the ovary characterized by the presence of small papillary projections in the inner surface of the cysts.

MONDO:0003873.text: A benign serous neoplasm characterized by the presence of papillary proliferations on the surface of the ovary.

MONDO:0003874.text: A serous adenocarcinoma that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of a papillary architectural pattern.

MONDO:0003875.text: A mature teratoma that arises from the central nervous system during childhood.

MONDO:0003876.text: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the eyelid.

MONDO:0003878.text: A uveal melanoma that arises from the choroid. It is the most common primary malignant intraocular tumor. It usually affects Caucasians of northern European descent. It usually remains asymptomatic for a long period. When signs and symptoms occur, they include blurred vision, visual field loss, floaters, and ocular pain. Tumor size is the most important factor that relates to prognosis.

MONDO:0003879.text: A malignant neoplasm of the ovary characterized by the presence of malignant glandular cells resembling endometrial cells in a fibrotic stroma.

MONDO:0003880.text: An infiltrating adenocarcinoma derived from ceruminous glands in the external auditory canal.

MONDO:0003881.text: An apocrine adenocarcinoma that arises from the sweat glands in the vulva.

MONDO:0003882.text: A usually aggressive malignant neoplasm arising from the central nervous system. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and collagenous stroma formation in a herringbone growth pattern.

MONDO:0003884.text: A benign adipose tissue neoplasm of the rectum.

MONDO:0003885.text: A rare benign adipose tissue neoplasm arising from the wall of the colon and rectum.

MONDO:0003886.text: A benign neoplasm characterized by the presence of cystic structures lined by mucinous columnar epithelial cells in a fibrotic stroma.

MONDO:0003887.text: A benign neoplasm of the ovary characterized by the presence of glands with mucinous columnar epithelial cells in a fibrotic stroma.

MONDO:0003888.text: A malignant testicular mixed germ cell neoplasm that occurs during childhood. It is characterized by the presence of embryonal carcinoma and teratoma components.

MONDO:0003889.text: An invasive transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder characterized by the presence of clear cells.

MONDO:0003890.text: An invasive transitional cell carcinoma that arises from the urinary bladder urothelium.

MONDO:0003891.text: A signet ring cell carcinoma that involves the urinary bladder.

MONDO:0003892.text: A morphologic variant of lung adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of acinar structures composed of columnar or cuboidal cells. (NCI05)

MONDO:0003893.text: A benign epithelial neoplasm arising from the rete testis.

MONDO:0003894.text: A melanotic schwannoma that affects the mediastinum.

MONDO:0003895.text: An intermediate grade malignant bone-forming mesenchymal neoplasm with chondroblastic differentiation. It arises from the surface of the bone and affects the diaphysis or diaphyseal- metaphyseal portion of the long bones. A painless mass or swelling is the most common clinical sign. It is associated with a better prognosis than conventional osteosarcoma.

MONDO:0003896.text: A capillary hemangioma arising from the breast.

MONDO:0003897.text: A hemangioma characterized by the presence of epithelioid endothelial cells, arising from the breast.

MONDO:0003898.text: A myxoid chondrosarcoma occurring in children.

MONDO:0003899.text: A myxoid chondrosarcoma occurring in adults.

MONDO:0003900.text: A disease involving the connective tissue.

MONDO:0003901.text: A histologically benign tumor, usually cystic with a vascular mural nodule, that is most often found in the cerebellum though it has been reported at other sites within the neuraxis. It is associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease (VHL gene located on chr 3p25-26).

MONDO:0003902.text: A hemangioblastoma that involves the brainstem.

MONDO:0003903.text: A non-metastasizing, well circumscribed neoplasm that arises from the vagina and is characterized by the presence of a predominant benign mesenchymal component and benign glandular or squamous epithelial cells.

MONDO:0003904.text: A squamous cell lung carcinoma detectable by sputum cytology only. The primary tumor is undetectable radiographically or during bronchoscopy; therefore, it can not be assessed.

MONDO:0003905.text: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of extensive differentiation into endodermal type glandular structures.

MONDO:0003906.text: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of extensive differentiation into hepatic tissue.

MONDO:0003907.text: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of multiple dilated spaces lined by cells that resemble mesothelial cells. The dilated spaces coexist with columnar epithelial tissues.

MONDO:0003908.text: A meningioma that affects the clivus.

MONDO:0003909.text: A rare, benign neoplasm that arises from the Bartholin gland and is characterized by the presence of a fibromuscular stroma and glands lined by mucin-secreting epithelial cells, arranged in a lobular architecture.

MONDO:0003910.text: A melanoma arising from the choroid, ciliary body, or the iris. It is characterized by the presence of a mixture of spindle A melanoma cells, spindle B melanoma cells, and epithelioid melanoma cells.

MONDO:0003911.text: A mixed cell uveal melanoma that involves the ciliary body.

MONDO:0003912.text: A rare uveal melanoma that arises from the ciliary body. Patients may present with blurred vision, visual field loss, floaters, and ocular pain. The prognosis is usually poor.

MONDO:0003913.text: A mixed cell uveal melanoma that involves the optic choroid.

MONDO:0003915.text: A thymic epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic large, polygonal epithelial cells with large vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli. The neoplastic cells are arranged around perivascular spaces and along septa. Immature T-lymphocytes are also present. It may be associated with myasthenia gravis, pure red cell aplasia, and hypogammaglobulinemia. It is a tumor of moderate malignancy. The majority of cases occur in the anterior mediastinum as Masaoka stage I, stage II, or stage III tumors. Metastatic, stage IV tumors occur less frequently.

MONDO:0003916.text: An imbalanced nutritional status resulting from excessive intake of nutrients. Generally, overnutrition generates an energy imbalance between food consumption and energy expenditure leading to disorders such as obesity.

MONDO:0003917.text: An extranodal lymphoma that arises from the heart and/or the pericardium. The majority of the cases are diffuse large B-cell lymphomas. Patients may present with chest pain, heart failure, pericardial effusion, arrhythmia, or syncope.

MONDO:0003918.text: A WHO grade I meningioma characterized by the presence of small and medium sized vessels that predominate over the meningioma cells.

MONDO:0003921.text: A meningioma that affects the posterior foramen magnum.

MONDO:0003922.text: A carcinoma arising from the ovary. It is characterized by the presence of malignant epithelial cells with clear cytoplasm in a fibrotic stroma.

MONDO:0003923.text: A papilloma that arises from the ciliated respiratory mucosa that lines the ethmoid sinus. It is classified as inverted papilloma and oncocytic papilloma.

MONDO:0003924.text: A benign neoplasm that can arise from any of the adrenal cortical layers. It can be associated with the overproduction of glucocorticoids (Cushing's syndrome), androgenic or estrogenic steroids (adrenogenital syndrome), or mineralocorticoids (Conn's syndrome). (Sternberg Diagnostic Surgical Pathology, 3rd ed.)

MONDO:0003925.text: A benign neoplasm that arises from the ciliated respiratory mucosa that lines the ethmoid sinus. It results from the invagination and proliferation of epithelial cells in the underlying stroma.

MONDO:0003926.text: A schwannoma that involves the pleura.

MONDO:0003928.text: A morphologic variant of leiomyosarcoma arising from the uterus corpus. It is characterized by the presence of cellular pleomorphism, malignant cells with large nuclei, and a myxoid stroma.

MONDO:0003929.text: A benign neoplastic process characterized by the presence of multiple vestibular papillomas in the vulva.

MONDO:0003930.text: Stage 0 includes: 0a (Ta, N0, M0); 0is (Tis, N0, M0). Ta: Noninvasive papillary carcinoma. Tis: Carcinoma in situ: "flat tumor". N0: No regional lymph node metastasis. M0: No distant metastasis. (AJCC 6th and 7th eds.)

MONDO:0003931.text: An astrocytoma that arises from the visual pathway and occurs during childhood.

MONDO:0003932.text: A glioma affecting the optic tract and occurring in childhood.

MONDO:0003933.text: An uncommon malignant neoplasm that arises from the chest wall bones. Representative examples include chondrosarcoma, osteosarcoma, and Ewing sarcoma/peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor.

MONDO:0003934.text: An adenocarcinoma of the breast characterized by the presence of two intermingled cellular components: cells with abundant granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm, and cells with abundant cytoplasm containing fine empty vacuoles.

MONDO:0003935.text: A rare breast adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of neoplastic oncocytic cells. The oncocytic cells comprise more than 70 percent of the malignant cellular population.

MONDO:0003936.text: An invasive adenocarcinoma of the breast with a favorable prognosis. It is composed of tubular structures lined by a single layer of epithelium.

MONDO:0003939.text: A disease involving the muscle tissue.

MONDO:0003940.text: A disease that presents as vertebral osteonecrosis typically affecting a thoracic vertebra with compression deformity, intravertebral vacuum cleft, and exaggerated kyphosis weeks to months after a minor traumatic injury.

MONDO:0003943.text: A rare benign slow growing adipose tumor, characterized by the presence of polygonal brown fat cells with abundant cytoplasm, that arises within the nervous system.

MONDO:0003944.text: A benign smooth muscle neoplasm arising endobronchially. It is characterized by the presence of spindle cells with cigar-shaped nuclei, interlacing fascicles, and a whorled pattern.

MONDO:0003945.text: A locally aggressive hemangioma that arises from the bone. It is characterized by the presence of epithelioid endothelial cells.

MONDO:0003946.text: An adenoma that arises from the vagina and is characterized by a villous architectural pattern.

MONDO:0003947.text: A primary immune deficiency disorder characterized by defective CD40 signaling; via B cells affecting class switch recombination (CSR) and somatic hypermutation.

MONDO:0003948.text: A hemangioma arising from the cerebral hemisphere.

MONDO:0003950.text: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the nipple

MONDO:0003951.text: A hemangioma arising from the skin of the scrotum.

MONDO:0003952.text: A choriocarcinoma of the central nervous system that occurs in an adult.

MONDO:0003953.text: A choriocarcinoma that arises from the central nervous system and occurs during childhood.

MONDO:0003954.text: An angiokeratoma that is located on the scrotum or vulva.

MONDO:0003955.text: A benign, usually solitary, well circumscribed multicystic neoplasm that arises from the breast and typically affects young females. The cysts are lined by papillary proliferations that contain epithelial and myoepithelial layers. In a minority of cases, atypia may be present.

MONDO:0003958.text: An immature teratoma that arises from the central nervous system and occurs during childhood.

MONDO:0003959.text: A poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma that arises from the breast. It is characterized by the presence of large neuroendocrine cells and high mitotic activity.

MONDO:0003960.text: A large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma that involves the lung(s).

MONDO:0003962.text: Froelich syndrome is characterized by obesity and hypogonadism due to a hypothalamic-pituitary disorder. The hypothalamus is a part of the brain where certain functions such as sleep cycles and body temperature are regulated. The pituitary is a gland that makes hormones that affect growth and the functions of other glands in the body. Froehlich syndrome is acquired(i.e., not thought to be inherited or genetic). This syndrome appears to affect males more commonly. The term 'Froelich syndrome' is rarely used today.

MONDO:0003963.text: This is usually an oligoclonal CD8+ lymphocytic infiltration of various organs.

MONDO:0003964.text: A disorder characterized by non-neoplastic bone formation in soft tissues. It usually follows blunt trauma and bleeding in the deep soft tissues.

MONDO:0003965.text: A rare neuropsychiatric disorder whose primary feature is the delusion that relatives or close acquaintances are not the persons that they are known to be. Visual recognition appears intact but familiar persons are thought be imposters, that is, they appear similar or identical to known individuals but are not. Most cases are seen in the context of a psychotic state. However, if manifested post-traumatically, the cause is most likely due to neurologic impairment. This disorder should be contrasted with prosopagnosia, in which an individual may not recognize a familiar person at all.

MONDO:0003966.text: A choriocarcinoma that arises from the testis and is characterized by the predominance of cytotrophoblastic and intermediate trophoblastic cells. Syncytiotrophoblastic cells are absent or not prominent.

MONDO:0003967.text: A bone osteosarcoma affecting multiple skeletal sites, with multifocal lesions discovered within 6 months of the appearance of the initial tumor. It has a poor prognosis.

MONDO:0003968.text: A bone osteosarcoma affecting multiple skeletal sites, with multifocal lesions discovered between 6 and 24 months after the appearance of the initial tumor. Patients with asynchronous tumors have a better prognosis than those with synchronous osteosarcomas.

MONDO:0003969.text: Disorders related or resulting from use of amphetamines.

MONDO:0003970.text: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the fundus of stomach.

MONDO:0003971.text: A carcinoma that arises from the pylorus.

MONDO:0003972.text: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the body of stomach.

MONDO:0003973.text: A morphologic variant of testicular seminoma characterized by the presence of seminoma cells arranged in tubular patterns and few lymphocytes.

MONDO:0003975.text: A carcinoma involving a male urethral gland.

MONDO:0003976.text: A type AB thymoma which is characterized by an aggressive clinical course (capsular invasion, infiltration of the surrounding tissues) and can metastasize.

MONDO:0003978.text: An aggressive, high-grade, and poorly differentiated carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the colon. It is characterized by the presence of malignant small cells.

MONDO:0003979.text: A mucinous cystic neoplasm that arises from the intrahepatic bile ducts.

MONDO:0003980.text: A rare intracranial schwannoma that affects the jugular foramen.

MONDO:0003982.text: Carcinoma that affects both breasts in a simultaneous or non-simultaneous manner.

MONDO:0003983.text: Carcinoma that is detected in one breast within two months from the diagnosis of carcinoma in the other breast.

MONDO:0003984.text: A rare benign adipose tissue neoplasm of the internal auditory canal, often presenting as an acoustic tumor. It may be intermixed with the vestibulocochlear nerve and may adhere to adjacent structures.

MONDO:0003985.text: A lymphoma that affects the structures of the chest wall. The majority of cases are diffuse large B-cell lymphomas.

MONDO:0003987.text: A rare non-Hodgkin or Hodgkin lymphoma that arises in and is confined to the lung at the time of diagnosis.

MONDO:0003988.text: A rare lymphoma that arises from the bone or soft tissue of the sternum.

MONDO:0003989.text: A rare, malignant germ cell tumor arising from the ovary. It is characterized by the presence of embryoid bodies which resemble early embryos.
