MONDO:1030000.text: Any hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia which is accompanied by cystic structures in the kidneys, and in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the PMM2 promoter.

MONDO:1030002.text: A developmental disorder affecting the growth and development of the proximal end of the femur (thigh bone) near the hip joint characterized by avascular necrosis of the femoral head, cystic changes of the femoral head, and/or sclerosis of the femoral head. It is a relatively milder form of the other skeletal disorders associated with COL2A1.

MONDO:1030003.text: A disease caused by infection with Mycoplasmoides.

MONDO:1030004.text: A rare clinical disorder characterized by at least three recurrent episodes of meningitis associated with spontaneous recovery with or without antiviral therapy. Herpes simplex virus type 2 has frequently been implicated in the setting of this illness. RBLM is rare with prevalence rates estimated at 2 per 100,000 persons.

MONDO:1030005.text: A somatic mosaic condition caused by a postzygotic mutation (c.1234 C>T p.Leu412Phe) in the SMO gene. Two overlapping clinical syndromes associated with this variant in SMO have been reported; Curry-Jones Syndrome (MIM:601707) and Happle-Tinschert Syndrome. The syndrome is characterized by cutaneous and skeletal manifestations such as linear hypo‐ or hyperpigmented lesions, basaloid follicular hamartomas, palmoplantar pitting, atrophoderma, hypertrichosis, polydactyly or syndactyly, rib anomalies (rudimentary ribs), and limb‐length anomalies. Craniofacial and dental abnormalities such as dysmorphic facies, macrocephaly, craniosynostosis, jaw tumors (ameloblastoma) have also been reported. Additional abnormalities impacting the gastrointestinal, cerebral, ophthalmic, and gonadal organs should also be considered. Some of these features include anal anomaly, colonic adenocarcinoma, severe constipation, myelofibrosis and smooth muscle hamartomas, malrotation, medulloblastoma, cerebral malformations, developmental delay, cataract, microphthalmia, coloboma, glaucoma, and cryptorchidism.

MONDO:1030006.text: Happle-Tinschert syndrome (HTS) is a rare, sporadic, multisystem disorder characterized by hypo- and hyperpigmented skin patches following Blaschko's lines, plus acral skeletal and other abnormalities and is characterized by basaloid follicular hamartomas. HTS is caused by a postzygotic mutation in the SMO gene (c.1234C>T, p.Leu412Phe).

MONDO:1030007.text: A hypertensive disorder that is characterized by marked elevation in blood pressure, such as systolic blood pressure greater than 180 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure greater than 110 mmHg, and without evidence of target organ damage, such as pulmonary edema, cardiac ischemia, neurologic deficits, or acute renal failure.

MONDO:1030008.text: A mitral valve disorder characterized by incomplete valve closure.

MONDO:1030009.text: An atrial fibrillation disorder characterized by continuous atrial fibrillation that lasts for more than seven days.

MONDO:1030010.text: A cerebrovascular disorder characterized by an abnormal narrowing of a precerebral artery.

MONDO:1030011.text: An atrial fibrillation disorder characterized by intermittent atrial fibrillation that lasts less than seven days from onset.

MONDO:1030015.text: A porphyria disorder that is acquired during the lifetime of the individual.

MONDO:1030016.text: A schwannomatosis that causes a predisposition to develop multiple schwannoma. It is diagnosed when an individual does not meet criteria for NF2-related schwannomatosis, SMARCB1-related schwannomatosis, or LTZR1-related schwannomatosis and both of the following molecular features exist: a loss of heterozygosity (LOH) of the same chromosome 22q markers in two anatomically distinct tumors or hybrid nerve sheath tumors and a different NF2 pathogenic variant in each tumor which cannot be detected in unaffected tissue.

MONDO:1040001.text: Any developmental defect during embryogenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TP63 gene. This disease is characterized by variable ectodermal dysplasia, limb defects, and orofacial clefting.

MONDO:1040002.text: Any overgrowth syndrome resulting from pathogenic gain-of-function variants in the PIK3CA gene. The variants can be germline or somatic

MONDO:1040003.text: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variation in the KCND2 gene. This disorder is characterized by early-onset global developmental delay with impaired motor, speech and cognitive development. Patients often present muscle hypotonia, and less frequently, developmental epileptic encephalopathy, visual impairment and physical dysmorphisms.

MONDO:1040004.text: Any overgrowth syndrome resulting from pathogenic gain-of-function variants in the PIK3R2 gene. The variants can be germline or somatic

MONDO:1040005.text: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the PRPF19 gene. This disorder is characterised by developmental, motor and speech delay, and facial dysmorphisms. Most patients present mild to moderate intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder or autistic features, and hypotonia. Other phenotypes observed less frequently include seizures, and visual and cardiac abnormalities.

MONDO:1040006.text: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CTR9 gene. This disorder is characterised by varying degrees of intellectual disability, neurodevelopmental delay, hypotonia, fatigability, behavioral abnormalities including autism spectrum disorder, anxiety and aggressive behavior, cardiac anomalies, and mild facial dysmorphism.

MONDO:1040007.text: A rare congenital brain disorder characterized by complete or almost near-complete unilateral absence of the cortical cortex, which is filled by a sac of cerebrospinal fluid. The presumed cause is a prenatal vascular disruption with occlusion of the carotid artery territories ipsilateral to the damaged brain.

MONDO:1040008.text: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variation in the CAMK2D gene. This disorder is characterised by intellectual disability, speech and motor delay, behavioural problems and dilated cardiomyopathy. Patients often present brain structural anomalies and hypotonia, and less frequently, seizures.

MONDO:1040009.text: Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TRIP11 gene. Reduced protein function in TRIP11 causes a spectrum of skeletal symptoms from a more mild phenotype, called ondontochondrodysplasia, with features including short stature and joint laxity to a more severe phenotype, called achondrogenesis type 1A, which presents as a lethal prenatal or neonatal skeletal dysplasia. The clinical severity of achondrogenesis compared to ondontochondrodysplasia is related to the residual function of the gene which is not currently possible to anticipate based on genotype alone. The phenotype cannot fully be predicted by genotype alone, evidenced by variants being reported with both phenotypes.

MONDO:1040010.text: Van der Woude syndrome, popliteal pterygium syndrome, cleft lip with or without palate, or a spectrum of one or two of those conditions in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the IRF6 gene.

MONDO:1040011.text: A human disorder which results from a tear in one of the major cervicocerebral arteries, allowing blood to enter the wall of the artery and split its layers. Pathogenesis typically leads to either stenosis or aneurysmal dilatation of the vessel.

MONDO:1040012.text: Any human disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the PI4KA gene. This disease is characterized primarily by neurologic dysfunction (limb spasticity, developmental delay, intellectual disability, seizures, ataxia, nystagmus), gastrointestinal manifestations (multiple intestinal atresia, inflammatory bowel disease), and combined immunodeficiency (leukopenia, variable immunoglobulin defects). Age of onset is typically antenatal or in early childhood; individuals can present with any combination of these features. Rare individuals present with later-onset hereditary spastic paraplegia. Brain MRI findings can include hypomyelinating leukodystrophy, cerebellar hypoplasia/atrophy, thin or dysplastic corpus callosum, and/or perisylvian polymicrogyria.

MONDO:1040014.text: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variation in the PPFIA3 gene. This disorder is characterised by developmental delay and intellectual disability. Most patients present variable additional features, including dysmorphisms, microcephaly or macrocephaly, hypotonia, autism spectrum disorder or autistic features, abnormal electroencephalogram, and epilepsy.

MONDO:1040015.text: An infectious disease characterized by life-threatening organ dysfunction due to a dysreguated host response.

MONDO:1040016.text: A cerebrovascular disorder characterized by an abnormal narrowing of a cerebral artery.

MONDO:1040017.text: An intestinal disorder characterized by an opening in the intestine to some epithelial surface.

MONDO:1040018.text: A disorder that is transmitted via X-linked inheritance and involves more than one phenotype associated with the central nervous system, including but not limited to intellectual disability, autism, and seizures (epilepsy), and also a distinctive pattern of other features including dysmorphisms and/or congenital malformations.

MONDO:1040019.text: A bacterial disease caused by infection with Enterococcus.

MONDO:1040020.text: A bacterial infectious disease caused by methicillin-susceptible staphylococcus aureus.

MONDO:1040021.text: Any postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the CHRNE gene.

MONDO:1040022.text: Group of rare heritable connective tissue disorders, characterized by a variable degree of short stature, skeletal dysplasia, joint laxity, cutaneous anomalies, dysmorphism, heart malformation, and developmental delay. The LK genes encode for enzymes that add glycosaminoglycan chains onto proteoglycans via a common tetrasaccharide linker region.

MONDO:1040023.text: A group of rare genetic conditions caused by variants in the NDUFB11 gene. Presentation is heterogenous including neurologic, cardiac, ocular, and dermatological abnormalities.

MONDO:1040024.text: A demyelinating disease of the central nervous system characterized by the presence of a demyelinating event (optic neuritis, myelitis, acute/multiphasic encephalomyelitis, cerebral or polyfocal deficits, brainstem or cerebellar deficits, and/or cerebral cortical encephalitis), a positive myelin oligodendrocyte glycorotein-IgG test, and exclusion of an alternative diagnosis like MS.

MONDO:1040026.text: A malignant neoplasm that has spread to the brain from another anatomic site.

MONDO:1040027.text: An array of connective tissue disorders characterized by joint instability and chronic pain. Fatigue and other systemic symptoms that affect daily function may occur as well. These diseases are scored using the Beighton scoring system and one of more secondary musculoskeletal manifestations including post-traumatic symptoms, pain, altered proprioception, and a variety of other characteristics like pes planus, kyphosis, scoliosis, or joint misalignment.

MONDO:1040028.text: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the PDE6C gene.

MONDO:1040029.text: An autoinflammatory disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the Sharpin gene.

MONDO:1040030.text: A susceptibility or predisposition to Parkinsons disease in which the cause of the disease is the presence of a monoallelic pathogenic variant or risk allele in the GBA1 gene.

MONDO:1040031.text: A spectrum of diseases related to monoallelic variants in DYNC1H1 and characterized by variable neuromuscular and/or neurodevelopmental presentations. While not absolute, there appear to be genotype-phenotype correlations based on the location of the variant. Patients with variants in the stem domain of DYNC1H1 have been reported with a predominantly neuromuscular presentation, including congenital myopathy, spinal muscular atrophy, Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT), and less frequently, intellectual disability and autism. Patients with variants in the motor domain predominantly present with neurodevelopmental presentations including intellectual disability, seizures, malformations of cortical development (abnormal brain MRI findings such as pachygyria, heterotopias, enlarged ventricles, hypoplasia of CC, brain stem, cerebellum), autism, and less frequently, neuromuscular phenotypes.

MONDO:1040032.text: A human mesomelic and rhizo-mesomelic dysplasia characterized by marked mesomelic shortening of the lower limbs, cutaneous syndactyly and nail abnormalities (placed on the palmar side of the finger, dysplastic or absent) in hands and feet due mutations in EN1 gene. Other clinical features may include genitourinary abnormalities (including bilateral cryptorchidism, vesicoureteral reflux, hydronephrosis, hypoplastic labia majora), spasticity and seizures.

MONDO:1040033.text: A congenital muscular dystrophy due to dystroglycanopathy characterized by a wide phenotypic spectrum which includes hypotonia and muscular weakness present at birth or early infancy, delayed or arrested motor development, and normal intellectual abilities with normal (or only mild abnormalities) neuroimaging studies. Feeding difficulties, joint and spinal deformities, and respiratory insufficiency may be associated. Decreased alpha-dystroglycan on immunohistochemical muscle staining and elevated serum creatine kinase are observed.

MONDO:1040034.text: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the PDE6G gene.

MONDO:1040035.text: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the LRIT3 gene.

MONDO:1040036.text: Any retinopathy caused by an autosomal dominant variant in the IMPG1 gene.

MONDO:1040037.text: Any retinopathy caused by autosomal recessive variants in the IMPG1 gene.

MONDO:1040038.text: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the TTLL5 gene.

MONDO:1040039.text: Any ciliopathy caused by monoallelic, biallelic, or hemizygous variants in the OFD1 gene. This disease is characterized by a broad range of phenotypes including Joubert syndrome, orofaciodigital syndrome, retinitis pigmentosa, and primary ciliary dyskinesia.

MONDO:1040040.text: Any isolated retinopathy caused by variants in the HGSNAT gene.

MONDO:1040041.text: Any exudative vitreoretinopathy caused by a variant in the FZD4 gene.

MONDO:1040042.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the BBS7 gene.

MONDO:1040043.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the BBS1 gene.

MONDO:1040044.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the BBS4 gene.

MONDO:1040045.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the BBS12 gene.

MONDO:1040046.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the LZTFL1 gene.

MONDO:1040047.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the BBS5 gene.

MONDO:1040048.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the BBS2 gene.

MONDO:1040049.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the TTC8 gene.

MONDO:1040050.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the MKKS gene.

MONDO:1040051.text: Any retinopathy caused by a variant in the IMPDH1 gene.

MONDO:1040052.text: Any retinopathy caused by autosomal recessive variants in the PROM1 gene.

MONDO:1040053.text: Any retinopathy caused by an autosomal dominant variant in the PROM1 gene.

MONDO:1040054.text: Any congenital disorder of glycosylation caused by variants in the DHDDS gene.

MONDO:1040055.text: Any retinopathy caused by a variant or variants in the PRPH2 gene.

MONDO:1040056.text: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the PROM1 gene.

MONDO:1040063.text: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the KCNV2 gene.

MONDO:1040064.text: Any retinopathy caused by a variant in the CRX gene.

MONDO:1040065.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the ARL6 gene.

MONDO:1040066.text: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the REEP6 gene.

MONDO:1040068.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the MKS1 gene.

MONDO:1040070.text: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the SPATA7 gene.

MONDO:1050000.text: Folliculitis of the beard and/or mustache areas caused by a bacterial infection, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus.

MONDO:1060001.text: Myasthenia gravis characterized by the presence of autoantibodies against the muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (AChR) in the serum, which damage the postsynaptic neuromuscular junction and cause skeletal muscle weakness and fatigue.

MONDO:1060002.text: Myasthenia gravis in which the muscles around the eyes are affected, that typically presents with ptosis and/or diplopia due to ophthalmoplegia

MONDO:1060003.text: Myasthenia gravis characterized by the presence of autoantibodies against muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) in the serum

MONDO:1060004.text: Myasthenia gravis characterized by the absence of detectable pathogenic auto-antibodies against acetylcholine receptor (AChR), muscle-specific tyrosine kinases (MuSK), and/or low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 4 (LRP4) in the sera.

MONDO:1060006.text: Myasthenia gravis in which muscle weakness affects one or more skeletal muscle groups outside the extraocular muscles

MONDO:1060107.text: Any disorder of oxysterol accumulation caused by biallelic loss of function variants in the CYP7B1 gene. A disorder of oxysterol accumulation is a condition where there is an abnormal buildup of oxysterols, which are oxidized cholesterol derivatives, in the body.

MONDO:1060108.text: A rare neurologic disease characterized by neonatal hypotonia, global developmental delay, feeding difficulties, and often seizures or seizure-like episodes. Other frequently observed signs and symptoms include variable dysmorphic features, myopathic facies, respiratory problems, and visual abnormalities, such as strabismus or esotropia. Brain imaging may show delayed myelination and other white matter abnormalities.

MONDO:1060109.text: A spectrum of disease associated with loss or disrupted function of the PLEC gene. These disorders primarily affect the skin and muscles, leading to a range of symptoms including skin blistering (EBS), progressive muscle weakness (muscular dystrophy), and other complications.

MONDO:1060110.text: A disorder caused by haploinsufficiency of HDAC4 and is characterized by brachydactyly type E, variable mild to moderate intellectual disability, seizures, autism spectrum disorder, short stature, obesity, and facial dysmorphism. Individuals with the gain of functions variants typically do not have brachydactyly and do have more consistent intellectual disability.

MONDO:1060111.text: A susceptibility or predisposition to myeloid neoplasms in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the SAMD9L gene. This condition is characterized by variable presentations of ataxia and cytopenia, myelodysplastic syndrome, monosomy 7 (acute myelogenous leukemia), and bone marrow failure.

MONDO:1060113.text: A genital ulcer characterized by the rapid onset of painful, necrotic ulcerations of the vulva or lower vagina. It typically occurs in sexually inactive adolescent females or young females and may be preceded by influenza-like or mononucleosis-like symptoms. Acute genital ulceration has been associated with acute Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection or other viral and bacterial infections. However, in many cases a cause cannot be determined.

MONDO:1060115.text: Any ciliopathy in which the cause of the disease is a variant in the TUBB4B gene. Please note that patient diagnoses can include disorders such as Leber congenital amaurosis and/or primary ciliary dyskinesia.

MONDO:1060116.text: Any mitochondrial disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FDXR gene.

MONDO:1060117.text: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MYCBP2 gene. This condition is characterized by variable corpus callosum defects consistent with dysgenesis, and a broad spectrum of neurobehavioural deficits including developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autistic features.

MONDO:1060120.text: An optic atrophy in which the cause of the disease is monoallelic or biallelic variants in the ACO2 gene. ACO2 is a mitochondrial protein and thus, in addition to the optic atrophy features, features of this disease include abnormal mitochondrial morphology and can affect other organ systems. Extraocular features can include ataxia, spastic paraplegia, CNS abnormalities, neurodevelopmental phenotypes, and retinal degeneration.

MONDO:1060121.text: An invasive adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of focal or extensive transformation of malignant glandular cells to squamous epithelial cells.

MONDO:1060122.text: An autosomal dominant disease caused by variants in the ALG8 gene that is characterized by incomplete penetrance and a range of clinical manifestations, spanning from individuals with normal kidneys to those with numerous kidney cysts and chronic kidney disease (CKD). While the common presentation involves a limited number of kidney cysts and maintained kidney function, severe polycystic liver disease (PLD) with minimal kidney involvement (ADPLD) can also occur.

MONDO:1060123.text: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variation in the GRIN1 gene. It is characterized by mild-to-profound developmental delay/intellectual disability (DD/ID) in all affected individuals. Other common manifestations are epilepsy, muscular hypotonia, movement disorders, spasticity, feeding difficulties, and behavior issues. A subset of individuals show a malformation of cortical development consisting of extensive and diffuse bilateral polymicrogyria.

MONDO:1060125.text: A rare, life-threatening fetal condition resulting complete or partial obstruction of the fetal upper airways. Laryngeal atresia is the most frequent cause, but other etiologies, such as laryngeal cyst, subglottic stenosis or atresia, tracheal atresia, and laryngeal or tracheal agenesis are also included.

MONDO:1060126.text: A form of Cushing syndrome caused by prolonged exposure or excessive use of cortisteroids, usually from medications taken to treat other conditions.

MONDO:1060132.text: Any orofacial cleft in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ARHGAP29 gene.
MONDO:1060132.references: https://clinicalgenome.org/affiliation/40059/, PMID:23008150, PMID:25704602, PMID:28029220, PMID:33150183, PMID:36902838, PMID:37589029, PMID:39506048

MONDO:1060134.text: Any cardiovascular disease resulting from atherosclerosis.

MONDO:1060136.text: A group of disorders caused by a variation in PIK3R1 gene that produces a structurally altered but present p85α protein, disrupting PI3K signaling and leading to features such as immune deficiency, autoimmunity, short stature, and distinct facial and skeletal features.

MONDO:1060138.text: A group of neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders caused by pathogenic variants in genes encoding subunits of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor, including GRIN1, GRIN2A, GRIN2B, and GRIN2D. These disorders are associated with a spectrum of symptoms such as developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy, movement disorders, speech and language impairment, and neuropsychiatric features. The clinical presentation and severity vary depending on the specific gene and mutation involved.

MONDO:1060139.text: A group of neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders caused by variants in the GRIN2A gene, characterized by a broad spectrum of symptoms including developmental delay or intellectual disability, epilepsy, speech and language impairments, movement disorders, and neuropsychiatric features.

MONDO:1060140.text: Any developmental and/or epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep in which the cause of the disease is a variation in GRIN2A gene.

MONDO:1060141.text: Any rolandic epilepsy-speech dyspraxia syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in GRIN2A gene.

MONDO:1060142.text: Any self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes in which the cause of the disease is a variation in GRIN2A gene.

MONDO:1060144.text: A digenic form of retinitis pigmentosa resulting from a mutation in the PRPH2 gene and a null mutation of the ROM1 gene, leading to progressive degeneration of the retina and vision loss.

MONDO:1060145.text: A Leber congenital amaurosis that is caused by a variation in the PRPH2 gene.

MONDO:1060146.text: Any Pfeiffer syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FGFR1 gene.

MONDO:1060147.text: Any Pfeiffer syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FGFR2 gene.

MONDO:1060148.text: A rare iatrogenic disease characterized by paradoxical nasal obstruction and symptoms including air hunger and suffocation-like breathing sensation, nasal dryness and crusting, burning pain or cold airflow sensation, impaired sleep and cognitive function and severe anxiety and depression, and typically occurs after surgical reduction or removal of nasal turbinates.

MONDO:1060149.text: A rare semidominant genetic skeletal disorder caused by a variation in ACAN gene, characterized by short stature with variable phenotypic features which may include osteochondritis dissecans, advanced bone age, early-onset arthritis, and/or features consistent with spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, Kimberley type caused by a single allele whereas biallelic variation can cause spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, aggrecan type.

MONDO:1060150.text: A disease characterized by a spectrum of cardiac and extracardiac phenotypes caused by a disease-causing variant in the NOTCH1 gene, inherited in an autosomal dominant manner. Affected individuals may present with congenital heart defects, bicuspid aortic valve, aortic valve stenosis, thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection, anomalies in brain structure, intracranial or posterior circulation vascular anomalies, cutaneous vascular malformations, cutis marmorata, and/or a phenotype compatible with Adams-Oliver syndrome (i.e. cutis aplasia, terminal limb defects, skull ossification defects).

MONDO:1060151.text: A schizoaffective disorder marked by episodes of hypomania or mania and sometimes major depression.

MONDO:1060152.text: A schizoaffective disorder marked by episodes of only major depression.

MONDO:1060153.text: A form of multiple symmetric lipomatosis accompanied by partial lipodystrophy (loss of subcutaneous fat in other regions), with or without peripheral neuropathy. Nearly all reported cases have been observed in individuals who are homozygous for the p.Arg707Trp variant in the MFN2 gene.

MONDO:1060154.text: A skeletal ciliopathy caused by a mutation in INTU gene and is characterized by facial dysmorphism, tongue nodules, developmental delay, and polydactyly. Some individuals may also present with short stature, or other variable syndromic findings.

MONDO:1060159.text: A movement disorder characterized by having one or more different types of movement disorders, such as abnormal muscle tone, abnormal degree of movement, dystonia or torsion, which may occur with or without neurodevelopmental features, such as developmental delay or intellectual disability.

MONDO:1060161.text: A form of distal renal tubular acidosis that is inherited.

MONDO:1060162.text: A form of distal renal tular acidosis that develops secondary to another condition, usually disease or drug.

MONDO:1060165.text: Any neutropenia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ELANE gene.

MONDO:1060166.text: A rare autoimmune disease of early childhood, marked by the simultaneous or sequential immune attack on red blood cells and liver cells.

MONDO:1060169.text: Hereditary cancer predisposition due to variation(s) in the HAVCR2 gene, which confers the predisposition to susceptibility to subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma (SPTCL) and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). Affected individuals typically present with multiple subcutaneous nodules and systemic B symptoms.

MONDO:1060171.text: A diffuse midline glioma characterized by H3 K27 alteration and usually either a histone H3 K27M mutation, an EGFR mutation, or aberrant overexpression of EZHIP. The prognosis is poor.

MONDO:1060172.text: Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in FAM111A gene.
MONDO:1060172.references: https://clinicalgenome.org/affiliation/40106/, MONDO:patterns/disease_series_by_gene, PMID:23684011, PMID:28138333, PMID:33263187, PMID:33750016, PMID:35205306, PMID:36916904, PMID:38679371, PMID:39501122

MONDO:1060173.text: Any autosomal dominant filamin related bone disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in FLNB gene.

MONDO:1060174.text: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1QA gene.

MONDO:1060176.text: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1S gene.

MONDO:1060177.text: A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused by the variants in the RNU2-2 gene, in which most reported variants are de novo. It is characterized by global developmental delay, hypotonia, impaired intellectual development, microcephaly, autistic behavior, and characteristically complex seizures.

MONDO:1060178.text: An autoimmune disorder that involves a constellation of psychiatric and neurologic symptoms that present simultaneously and in rapid onset, the cause or causes of which are unknown. Although the cause is still under investigation, the manifestations may follow a recent infection.

MONDO:1060179.text: A neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in RNU5B-1 gene and is characterized by global developmental delay, hypotonia, macrocephaly, failure to thrive, abnormality of the eye, seizures, and joint laxity

MONDO:1060180.text: A glioblastoma localized in the brain stem.

MONDO:1060182.text: Any propionic acidemia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in PCCA gene.

MONDO:1060183.text: Any propionic acidemia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in PCCB gene.

MONDO:1060184.text: Hereditary cancer predisposition due to variation(s) in the EGLN12 gene, which confers a predisposition to erythrocytosis and pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma.

MONDO:1060185.text: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the PLD4 gene.

MONDO:1060188.text: A variant of parapsoriasis characterized by round-to-oval plaques less than 5cm in diameter, and it rarely progresses.

MONDO:1060189.text: A variant of parapsoriasis characterized by erythematous-to-brown patches or thin plaques with fine scales larger than 5cm in diameter. It has a substantial risk to evolve to mycosis fungoides.

MONDO:1060190.text: A hereditary amyloidosis characterized by a spectrum of neurodegenerative and neurovascular phenotypes caused by pathogenic variant in the APP gene, resulting in an abnormal clearance of amyloid peptides, either by overproduction and decreased clearance of amyloid peptides, with deposition of amyloid in plaques and blood vessel walls. Affected individuals may present with progressive cognitive decline, cerebral vascular amyloidosis with white matter changes, and stroke with or without hemorrhage.

MONDO:1060191.text: Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the IFT74 gene.
MONDO:1060191.references: https://clinicalgenome.org/affiliation/40066, PMID:27486776, PMID:33531668, PMID:33748949, PMID:34539760, PMID:37315079, PMID:37555648

MONDO:1060192.text: A syndromic disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CASK gene. It is associated with a wide phenotypic spectrum ranging from mild-to-severe intellectual disability with or without nystagmus to moderate-to-profound intellectual disability and progressive microcephaly with pontine and cerebellar hypoplasia, often associated with seizures.

MONDO:1060193.text: An X-linked intelelctual disability in which the cause of the disease is hypomorphic CASK pathogenic variants. Affected individuals present with intellectual disability with or without congenital nystagmus. Additional features often include epilepsy, speech impairment, motor delay, and variable brain malformations. Phenotypic severity ranges from mild cognitive impairment to severe developmental disability.

MONDO:1060194.text: An autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome that results from defective lymphocyte homoestasis, and is caused by variants in the FAS gene. It is characterized by non-malignant lymphoproliferation, autoimmune disease, and lifelong increased risk for both Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

MONDO:1060195.text: A predisposition caused by a mutation in SH2B3 gene that presents with myeloproliferation and/or multi-organ autoimmunity.

MONDO:1060197.text: A heart disease that is present at birth that occurs with variable extracardiac laterality defects. Features of visceral heterotaxy are not always present but can include abnormal location of the organs within the thoracic, abdominal, or peritoneal cavities. Anatomic and functional problems can include intestinal malrotation leading to volvulus, biliary atresia, and various defects of the central nervous system, urinary tract, and skeleton.

MONDO:1060198.text: A stroke disorder caused by obstruction of blood flow to the brain, due to thrombotic (local blood clot formation) or embolic (due to a blood clot or other material traveling from another site) event.

MONDO:1060199.text: A stroke disorder caused by bleeding into the brain parenchyma or surrounding spaces. Hemorrhagic stroke includes intracerebral hemorrhage (bleeding within the brain tissue) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (bleeding in the space between the brain and the surrounding membrane).

MONDO:1060200.text: A form of hyperthyroidism caused by overproduction of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) due to pathology within the thyroid gland itself. Primary hyperthyroidism is characterized by low TSH levels and elevated T3/T4 levels.

MONDO:1060201.text: A form of hyperthyroidism caused by overproduction of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) due to pathology outside of the thyroid gland, namely in the hypothalamus or pituitary gland. Secondary hyperthyroidism is characterized by elevated TSH levels and elevated T3/T4 levels.

MONDO:1060202.text: A condition in which a single benign adenoma on the thyroid gland  autonomously secretes excessive thyroid hormone, leading to primary hyperthyroidism.

MONDO:1060203.text: A form of secondary hyperthyroidism caused by pathology in the hypothalamus leading to excessive stimulation of the pituitary gland and subsequent overproduction of TSH, resulting in elevated thyroid hormone levels.

MONDO:1060204.text: A disorder of the female reproductive system characterized by abnormalities in the menstrual cycle, including disturbances in timing, flow, or associated pain.

MONDO:1060205.text: A menstrual disorder characterized by pain during the menstrual cycle.

MONDO:1060206.text: A form of dysmenorrhea characterized by recurrent menstrual pain without any identifiable underlying pelvic pathology, representing a diagnosis of exclusion. Symptoms typically emerge within two years of menarche.

MONDO:1060207.text: A form of dysmenorrhea associated with suspected or clinically identifiable pelvic pathology, such as endometriosis, uterine fibroids, or adenomyosis.

MONDO:1060208.text: A form of amenorrhea defined by the absence of menstruation by the age of 15 years, or by 3 years after the onset of breast development (thelarche).

MONDO:1060209.text: A form of amenorrhea characterized by the absence of menses for 3 or more months in a woman with previously regular menstrual cycles, or 6 or more months in any woman who has had at least one previous spontaneous menstruation.

MONDO:1060210.text: A form of secondary amenorrhea caused by suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis without identifiable organic pathology, typically associated with energy deficiency, excessive exercise, psychological stress, or low body weight.

MONDO:1060211.text: A reproductive system disorder caused by a variation in the NR5A1 gene, and characterized by varying phenotypes, including partial or complete gonadal dysgenesis, ambiguous genitalia, and spermatogenic failure in the male, and premature ovarian failure and ovarian dysgenesis in the female.

MONDO:1060212.text: A syndromic disease caused by a variation in the CRYAB gene, and characterized by a spectrum of phenotypes including cardiomyopathy, cataract, and/or myopathy.

MONDO:1060213.text: A retinal drusen characterized by subretinal deposits located internal to the retinal pigment epithelium, composed of material aggregations in the subretinal space between photoreceptors and the retinal pigment epithelium. These deposits have a bluish-white appearance by biomicroscopy and appear as hyperreflective lesions above the retinal pigment epithelium on optical coherence tomography.

MONDO:1060214.text: An infertility disorder caused by variation in the SYCE1 gene. Affected males may present with non-obstructive azoospermia due to maturation arrest or meiotic failure, while affected females may present with primary ovarian insufficiency.

MONDO:1060215.text: A precancerous condition characterized by accumulation of some molecular alterations necessary for malignant transformation in a clonal proliferation of cells, representing an intermediate stage in carcinogenesis with increased risk of progression to invasive neoplasia.

MONDO:1060216.text: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TSEN2 gene. This condition is associated with intellectual disability, growth delay, hypotonia, motor delay, ataxia, vision issues, cardiac features (including left ventricular hypertrophy), and pulmonary complications (such as acute respiratory distress and edema). It is also linked to brain structural anomalies such as pontine and cerebellar hypoplasia, cortical atrophy, and dilated ventricles. Renal features include proteinuria, thrombotic microangiopathy, end-stage kidney disease, and high-severity hypertension.
MONDO:1060216.references: https://clinicalgenome.org/affiliation/40069/, PMID:18711368, PMID:20952379, PMID:23562994, PMID:32404165, PMID:38347586, PMID:38438125, PMID:38622473

MONDO:1060217.text: A rare hypophysitis characterized histologically by mixed inflammatory cell infiltrates consisting of foamy histiocytes, plasma cells, and small round mature lymphocytes infiltrating the anterior pituitary gland. The tissue often contains cystic-like areas of liquefaction filled with lipid-laden macrophages along with lymphocytes and plasma cells.

MONDO:1060218.text: A hypophysitis exhibiting histologic features of both xanthomatous and granulomatous hypophysitis, characterized by cholesterol clefts, haemosiderin deposits, multinucleated giant cells, macrophage accumulation and fibrous proliferation.

MONDO:1060219.text: A rare hypophysitis defined histologically by extensive necrosis of pituitary tissue surrounded by lymphocytes, plasma cells, and eosinophils.

MONDO:1060220.text: A rare subtype of split cord malformation characterized by each hemicord contained in its own dural sac, typically with an intervening bony or cartilaginous septum.

MONDO:1060221.text: A rare subtype of split cord malformation characterized by both hemicords included in the same single dural sac. An intradural intervening mesenchymal septum may be present.

MONDO:1060222.text: A rare intermediate form of split cord malformation characterized by both hemichords encapsulated in a single dural sac with presence of an incomplete ventral or dorsal bony spur.

MONDO:1060223.text: Any hereditary disease caused by a variation in the RNU12 gene, resulting in abnormal splicing of pre-mRNA via the minor spliceosome. The phenotypic spectrum includes craniosynostosis-anal anomalies-porokeratosis (CDAGS) syndrome and autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia 33.

MONDO:1060224.text: A condition characterized by haploinsufficient levels of STAT5 protein due to reduced copy number or expression of the STAT5A and/or STAT5B genes, with consequent attenuation of STAT5-mediated cytokine signalling (including IL-7 and growth hormone pathways). This condition is also associated with altered lymphocyte homeostasis and modified susceptibility to lymphoma development.

MONDO:1060225.text: A skeletal muscle disorder caused by heterozygous multi-exon in-frame structural variants of TTN (TTNsv) that escape nonsense-mediated decay and result in expression of an internally deleted titin isoform with dominant-negative effects on sarcomere structure and function. Affected individuals typically present with congenital, childhood-onset, or adult-onset proximal and/or distal muscle weakness, often accompanied by joint contractures, and may develop respiratory involvement or cardiomyopathy.

MONDO:1060226.text: A disorder of sexual differentiation caused by biallelic variation in the MCM9 gene. Affected females (46,XX) may present with primary ovarian insufficiency or ovarian dysgenesis with short stature; affected males (46,XY) may present with non-obstructive azoospermia due to meiotic failure. Biallelic MCM9 variants have also been associated with predisposition to early-onset colorectal cancer, polyposis, gastric cancer, and germ cell tumors.

MONDO:1060227.text: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1QC gene.

MONDO:1060228.text: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1QB gene.

MONDO:1060229.text: An occupational illness caused by transdermal absorption of nicotine from handling wet, uncured tobacco leaves, presenting with nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, weakness, and other autonomic symptoms. Predominantly affects tobacco farmworkers during harvesting, topping, and curing activities.

MONDO:1060230.text: Any complex neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variationn in the BLOC1S1 gene. The disorder is characterized by intellectual disability, global developmental delay, leukodystrophy, optic atrophy, seizures, abnormal or delayed myelination, and spasticity; some individuals also present with mild features of hypopigmentation and ocular albinism.

MONDO:1060231.text: A predisposition to pituitary adenoma due to variation(s) in the AIP gene.

MONDO:1060232.text: A rare hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy characterized by the inability to perceive physical pain from birth. Affected individuals do not feel pain from injuries, burns, or infections and cannot detect harmful levels of heat, cold, or pressure, which can lead to repeated unrecognized injuries, impaired healing, and serious complications.

MONDO:1060233.text: A group of neurodevelopmental disorders caused by germline mutations in genes encoding subunits of the Mediator complex, a multi-protein assembly required for RNA polymerase II-dependent transcription. Shared phenotypic features include intellectual disability, speech and language delay, behavioral abnormalities, and variable structural brain anomalies.

MONDO:1060234.text: A platelet type bleeding disorder of autosomal dominant inheritance caused by a variation in the P2RY12 gene that exerts a dominant negative effect by disrupting receptor homodimerization, leading to markedly impaired adenosine diphosphate induced platelet aggregation despite normal receptor expression. Affected individuals may exhibit severe bleeding symptoms due to defective amplification of platelet activation signals.

MONDO:1060236.text: A genetic disorder caused by a variation in the GJB2 gene, primarily associated with hearing loss and/or deafness.

MONDO:1060237.text: Any Bernard-Soulier syndrome caused by the variation in the GP9 gene, marked by absent or markedly reduced GPIb-IX-V complex expression, resulting in impaired platelet adhesion and lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding. Platelets are large and functionally deficient, with severely reduced ristocetin-induced agglutination reflecting loss of functional GPIX within the receptor complex. Variants in GP9 disrupt synthesis or stability of the GPIX subunit, preventing proper assembly of the GPIb-IX-V complex and producing the characteristic bleeding phenotype.

MONDO:1060238.text: Any Bernard-Soulier syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the GP1BA gene, characterized by macrothrombocytopenia, reduced or absent expression of the GPIb-IX-V complex, and lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding. Affected individuals have large platelets with defective ristocetin-induced agglutination, reflecting the absence or dysfunction of GPIbα on the platelet surface. Variants in GP1BA impair production, trafficking, or incorporation of GPIbα into the receptor complex, preventing normal surface assembly and leading to the classic BSS adhesion defect.

MONDO:1060239.text: Any Bernard-Soulier syndrome caused by deficiency or dysfunction of GPIbβ, leading to markedly decreased GPIb-IX-V surface expression and impaired platelet adhesion. Platelets are enlarged and poorly responsive to ristocetin, consistent with severe reduction of the assembled receptor complex. Variants in GP1BB affect production or proper folding of the GPIbβ subunit, preventing formation of the full receptor complex and resulting in the characteristic Bernard-Soulier phenotype.

MONDO:1060240.text: Any disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the AARS2 gene.

MONDO:1060241.text: Any ectodermal dysplasia syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the EDA gene. Key features are hypohidrosis and hypotrichosis; the condition is also characterized by skin anomalies such as soft, thin, and dry skin, eczema, and pigmentation anomalies, as well as fine or brittle hair, dental anomalies such as hypodontia or oligodontia, vocal hoarseness, and hyperthermia susceptibility.
MONDO:1060241.references: https://clinicalgenome.org/affiliation/40059/, PMID:11343303, PMID:17066260, PMID:17256800, PMID:19623212, PMID:21357618, PMID:33205897, PMID:35923710

MONDO:1060243.text: Any hereditary disease in which the cause of the disease is a biallelic variation in the THG1L gene, encompassing a phenotypic spectrum that ranges from mild cerebellar ataxia with developmental delay to severe epileptic encephalopathy.

MONDO:1060244.text: Any genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a biallelic variation in the THG1L gene, characterized by profound developmental delay, microcephaly, intractable epilepsy, and cerebellar hypoplasia.

MONDO:1060245.text: Any nervous system disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SCN2A gene, which encodes the Nav1.2 sodium channel critical for neuronal function. SCN2A-related disorders span a broad phenotypic spectrum, from self-limited familial neonatal-infantile epilepsy through severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathies to later-onset epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability without seizures, and episodic ataxia. Because Nav1.2 is essential for brain development as well as neuronal excitability, the presentation is predominantly neurodevelopmental where developmental delay, intellectual disability, and autism spectrum disorder are the most consistent features across the spectrum, present even in the absence of seizures. Clinical severity is broadly associated with the functional effect of the variant on the Nav1.2 channel, with gain-of-function changes typically linked to early severe epilepsy and loss-of-function changes more often associated with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability or intellectual disability, although these relationships are complex and not fully understood.
MONDO:1060245.references: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9310-0163, https://scn2a.org/pdf/scn2arelated_disorders.pdf, PMID:28379373, PMID:31904126, PMID:31924505, PMID:38651838, PMID:40694750

MONDO:1060246.text: Any permanent neonatal diabetes mellitus in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the EIF2B1 gene, often accompanied by transient liver dysfunction.

MONDO:1060247.text: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the SMARCAL12 gene.

MONDO:1060248.text: An ultra-rare hereditary neurological disorder caused by a variation in the IMPDH2 gene, which encodes a key enzyme involved in guanine nucleotide biosynthesis and purine metabolism. The phenotype spans a spectrum from neurodevelopmental delay, intellectual disability, dystonia, tremor, and other movement abnormalities, with variable expressivity and age of onset.

MONDO:1060249.text: An atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor characterized by overexpression of genes in the sonic hedgehog (SHH) pathway (GLI2, BOC, PTCHD2, and MYCN).

MONDO:1060250.text: An atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor characterized by overexpression of the MYC gene.

MONDO:1060251.text: An atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor characterized by overexpression of melanosomal genes (TYR, TYRP, MITF, and OTX2).

MONDO:1060252.text: A central nervous system mesenchymal non-meningothelial tumor with a broad morphological spectrum, characterized by fusion of a FET family gene (usually EWSR1 and rarely FUS) with a member of the CREB family of transcription factors (CREB1, ATF1, or CREM). It includes entities previously termed intracranial angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma or intracranial myxoid mesenchymal tumor. It is usually located in the supratentorial brain and mostly affects children and young adults. There is a spectrum of clinical behaviors ranging from slowly growing tumors to rapid recurrences, and rarely metastases.

MONDO:1060253.text: A pineal body neoplasm that is a SMARCB1-deficient tumor of the brain, characterized by the presence of spindled and epithelioid cells with low-grade morphology that are embedded in a desmoplastic stroma alternating with various extents of loose myxoid matrix.

MONDO:1060254.text: A very rare, nonrhabdoid, intraventricular tumor with relatively favorable prognosis. It is characterized by the presence of neuroepithelial cells forming cribriform patterns, trabeculae, epithelial membrane antigen immunopositivity on epithelial surfaces, and loss of nuclear INI1 expression.

MONDO:1060256.text: An adult Refsum disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the PHYH gene.

MONDO:1060257.text: An ovarian serous carcinoma characterized by low-grade cytologic features, infrequent mitotic figures and slow tumor growth, which is thought to develop from a serous borderline ovarian tumor. It shows an activated mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway with KRAS and BRAF mutations and only rarely TP53 mutations, and is a distinct entity from high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma rather than a grade of it. It accounts for 2-5% of ovarian carcinomas and 5-10% of serous ovarian carcinomas.

MONDO:1060258.text: A phenylketonuria in which blood phenylalanine concentrations do not fall substantially (conventionally defined as a reduction of more than 30%) in response to an oral tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4; sapropterin dihydrochloride) loading test, so that treatment with BH4 is not effective and phenylalanine-restricted dietary management remains necessary.

MONDO:1060259.text: A disorder of phenylalanine metabolism caused by biallelic variants in the PAH gene, encompassing the full spectrum of phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency from mild hyperphenylalaninemia, which requires no treatment, to phenylketonuria, in which untreated blood phenylalanine concentrations warrant phenylalanine-restricted dietary treatment.

MONDO:1060260.text: An ossifying fibroma arising predominantly in children and young adults, comprising two histological variants: juvenile trabecular ossifying fibroma and psammomatoid ossifying fibroma.

MONDO:1060261.text: A juvenile ossifying fibroma predominantly arises in children and adolescents. It is characterized by prominent osteoid formation rimmed by osteoblasts in a fibrotic stroma. Patients usually present with painless jaw expansion that is associated with rapid growth and tooth displacement.

MONDO:1060262.text: A juvenile ossifying fibroma arises usually affects individuals in their second to fourth decades with no sex predilection. It is characterized by the presence of multiple ossicles resembling psammoma bodies in a hypercellular stroma.

MONDO:1060263.text: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the SMARCB1 gene. Pathogenic germline loss-of-function variants confer autosomal dominant predisposition to schwannomas, meningiomas, rhabdoid tumors and other rare types of tumors. The phenotype correlates with the variant's degree of loss of function: the schwannomatosis phenotype is more commonly observed with partial loss-of-function or hypomorphic variants, while the rhabdoid tumor phenotype is more commonly associated with complete loss-of-function variants.

MONDO:1060264.text: A neutropenia characterized by persistent absolute neutrophil count below 0.5 x 10^9/L lasting for at least 3 months, not explained by medication use, infection or another underlying condition, and associated with recurrent and potentially life-threatening bacterial infections. The major clinical subtypes include congenital, cyclic, idiopathic, and autoimmune neutropenia, which share common diagnostic evaluation, treatment strategies, and long-term follow-up.

MONDO:1060265.text: An idiopathic form of severe chronic neutropenia that cannot be classified as congenital, cyclic or autoimmune neutropenia, and is not explained by drug exposure, bone marrow failure, malignancy or systemic autoimmune disease. Symptoms are usually less severe than in congenital neutropenia, but infections can be life-threatening in some patients.

MONDO:1060266.text: An autoimmune form of severe chronic neutropenia in which neutrophil-specific antibodies increase the destruction of circulating neutrophils, in the absence of systemic autoimmune disease. It is most common in children aged 6 months to 4 years, and it can also occur in adults. Serious bacterial infections are infrequent.

MONDO:1060267.text: A skeletal system disorder caused by a variation in the GNAS gene, characterized by involvement of the skin, skeleton and certain endocrine organs. Fibrous dysplasia ranges from an isolated monostotic lesion to severe polyostotic disease. McCune-Albright syndrome is diagnosed when fibrous dysplasia occurs with at least one extra-skeletal feature, or when two or more extra-skeletal features occur alone. The condition is not inherited. The signs and symptoms associated with the disorder vary greatly from person to person, depending upon the specific body cells and tissues that are affected by the gene variant.

MONDO:1060269.text: An optic nerve disorder characterized by ischemic injury to the retrobulbar (posterior) portion of the optic nerve, presenting with sudden visual loss and an initially normal-appearing optic disc, in contrast to anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. It may be arteritic (due to giant cell arteritis), nonarteritic, or surgical (following a surgical procedure).

MONDO:1060270.text: An optic nerve disorder caused by closed or penetrating trauma to the face or head that injures the optic nerve, resulting in visual loss, often with an afferent pupillary defect.

MONDO:1060271.text: An optic nerve disorder caused by radiation necrosis of the anterior visual pathway, occurring as a late complication of radiotherapy for head and neck or intracranial tumours and resulting in acute, painless and usually irreversible visual loss. Onset is typically 10 to 20 months after treatment but ranges from 3 months to 9 years.

MONDO:1060272.text: An optic nerve disorder caused by mechanical compression of the optic nerve or chiasm along its course, for example by orbital or intracranial tumours, sinus mucoceles or thyroid eye disease, resulting in progressive visual loss.

MONDO:1060273.text: An ocular vascular disorder characterized by acute complete obstruction of the ophthalmic artery, a branch of the internal carotid artery, leading to severe ischemia of the globe and associated ocular tissues. It can resemble central retinal artery occlusion with additional choroidal ischemia, and may cause sudden and permanent visual loss.

MONDO:1060274.text: A vitreous and retinal disorder characterized by incomplete posterior vitreous detachment with persistent focal adhesion to the macula. This exerts anteroposterior traction that distorts foveal anatomy, causing structural changes such as foveal deformation, pseudocysts, macular schisis, cystoid macular edema, and subretinal fluid, with potential progression to a macular hole.

MONDO:1060275.text: A full-thickness macular hole that results from trauma, such as closed-globe or open-globe ocular injury, laser injury, surgical trauma, lightning strike or electrical shock. It occurs more often in young men, whereas idiopathic macular hole occurs more often in women older than 65 years.

MONDO:1060276.text: A uveitis occurring in individuals with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and its most frequent extra-articular manifestation. The most common form is chronic anterior uveitis, which is almost always asymptomatic in the initial stages, so screening of at-risk patients is essential.

MONDO:1060277.text: A glaucoma in which elevation of intraocular pressure results from an identifiable pathophysiological mechanism, such as intraocular inflammation, pigment dispersion, hemorrhage, trauma, corticosteroid use or elevated episcleral venous pressure, in contrast to primary glaucoma. Secondary glaucomas form a heterogeneous group of diseases.

MONDO:1060278.text: A secondary glaucoma that can develop in pigment dispersion syndrome, in which pigment released from the iris is deposited in the trabecular meshwork, reducing aqueous outflow and raising intraocular pressure, leading to glaucomatous optic neuropathy. It is usually diagnosed between 40 and 50 years of age and occurs more often in men.

MONDO:1060279.text: A secondary glaucoma in which optic nerve damage results from elevated intraocular pressure secondary to intraocular inflammation via trabecular inflammation/obstruction, steroid response, or synechial angle\nclosure in the setting of uveitis. Compared with primary open-angle glaucoma, it often has a more aggressive course, with very high intraocular pressure that waxes and wanes.

MONDO:1060280.text: A secondary glaucoma in which degenerated red blood cells (ghost cells), formed in the vitreous cavity after hemorrhage, pass forward into the anterior chamber and obstruct the aqueous outflow channels.

MONDO:1060281.text: A secondary glaucoma following intraocular hemorrhage, in which the trabecular meshwork is obstructed by fragments of hemolyzed red blood cells and hemoglobin-laden macrophages.

MONDO:1060282.text: A secondary glaucoma occurring in individuals with aniridia. Most affected eyes have open anterior chamber angles, and a minority have partial or complete angle closure.

MONDO:1060283.text: A form of primary angle-closure glaucoma caused by a large or anteriorly positioned ciliary body that leads to mechanical obstruction of the trabecular meshwork. It is most often found in young patients.

MONDO:1060284.text: A secondary open-angle glaucoma that develops in individuals with exfoliation syndrome. Exfoliation syndrome is associated with raised intraocular pressure in up to 44% of patients, making it the most commonly identifiable cause of secondary open-angle glaucoma.

MONDO:1060285.text: Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the FBN1 gene. This condition is characterized by short stature, delayed bone age, stiff joints, acromegaly, hip dysplasia, respiratory issues (including sleep apnea and asthma), short hands/feet, and facial anomalies (such as a long philtrum, bulbous nose, broad/depressed nasal bridge, thick lips, and elongation of the eyelashes).

MONDO:1060286.text: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CAMK2A gene.

MONDO:1060287.text: Any hereditary disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the NUS1 gene. Biallelic variants cause a congenital disorder of glycosylation. Heterozygous variants, including deletions, cause a complex neurological disorder with developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy including developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and progressive myoclonus epilepsy, and movement disorders including myoclonus, dystonia, ataxia, tremor and parkinsonism. Rare NUS1 variants have also been associated with Parkinson's disease.

MONDO:1060288.text: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SETBP1 gene. Variants in SETBP1 are associated with three different phenotypes: Schinzel-Giedion midface retraction syndrome, SETBP1 haploinsufficiency disorder, and SETBP1-related neurodevelopemental disorder caused by missense variant of unknown functional effect.

MONDO:1060289.text: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by a pathogenic missense variant of unknown functional effect that are not within or adjacent to the mutational hot spot in the SETBP1 gene. It is characterized by intellectual disability or developmental delay, speech and language delay, hypotonia and sleep issues, with variable seizures, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autistic traits, and a greater risk of orthopedic, gastrointestinal and heart issues than SETBP1 haploinsufficiency disorder. Inheritance is autosomal dominant and usually de novo.

MONDO:1060290.text: A multiple congenital anomalies/dysmorphic syndrome caused by homozygous loss-of-function variants in the ABL1 gene. It is characterized by multiple congenital malformations (wormian skull bones and brachydactyly) and distinctive facial dysmorphism (hypertelorism, prominent eyes, short, broad and flat nose, and macrostomia). It is allelic to, but clinically distinct from, congenital heart defects and skeletal malformations syndrome, which is caused by germline gain-of-function variants in ABL1.

MONDO:1060291.text: A form of familial long QT syndrome (LQTS) characterized by syncopal episodes and electrocardiographic abnormalities (QT prolongation, T-wave abnormalities and torsade de pointes (TdP) ventricular tachycardia).

MONDO:1060292.text: A long QT syndrome characterized by pathologic excessive prolongation of the QT interval, upon exposure to an environmental stressor, with reversion back to normal following removal of the stressor. It is most often due to specific drugs or metabolic abnormalities, such as hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia.

MONDO:1060293.text: An autosomal recessive acromesomelic dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a hypomorphic mutation in the BMPR1B gene. It belongs to a spectrum of skeletal dysplasias characterized by short stature, severe acromesomelic shortening of the limbs, and normal axial skeleton.

MONDO:1060294.text: A metastatic malignant neoplasm that originates from a primary malignant neoplasm of the breast and has spread to a secondary site.

MONDO:1060295.text: A metastatic malignant neoplasm in the liver that originates from a primary malignant neoplasm of the breast.

MONDO:1060296.text: A metastatic malignant neoplasm in the liver that originates from a primary malignant neoplasm of the colon.

MONDO:1060297.text: A malignant neoplasm that has spread to the liver from another (primary) anatomic site. Representative examples include carcinomas, lymphomas, melanomas, or sarcomas.

MONDO:1060298.text: A hereditary von Willebrand disease caused by pathogenic variation in VWF, resulting in abnormalities of von Willebrand factor quantity or function that impair hemostasis. VWF-related von Willebrand disease encompasses both quantitative deficiencies of VWF and qualitative defects affecting VWF-mediated platelet adhesion, platelet interaction, or factor VIII binding.

MONDO:1060299.text: VWF-related quantitative von Willebrand disease is characterized by decreased circulating VWF levels and impaired primary hemostasis, and includes both partial quantitative deficiency (von Willebrand disease type 1) and virtually complete quantitative deficiency (von Willebrand disease type 3).

MONDO:1060300.text: A VWF-related qualitative von Willebrand disease in which pathogenic variation in VWF reduces the ability of von Willebrand factor to support platelet tethering and adhesion under conditions of vascular injury.

MONDO:1060301.text: Epithelioid angiosarcoma is a highly aggressive endothelial cell malignancy, most commonly arising in the deep soft tissues, but a variety of primary sites, including the adrenals, thyroid, skin, and bone, are encountered.

MONDO:1060302.text: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SAT1 gene. Loss-of-function variants in SAT1 cause X-linked childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus.

MONDO:1060303.text: Any inborn error of immunity in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the DNAJC17 gene. It is characterized by retinopathy, combined immunodeficiency, and TNF-driven autoinflammation responsive to targeted TNF blockade.

MONDO:1060304.text: Any autosomal recessive severe congenital neutropenia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CSF3 gene.

MONDO:1060305.text: Any combined immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SIT1 gene.

MONDO:1060306.text: Any B cell deficiency in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SH3GL1 gene.

MONDO:1060307.text: Any hemophagocytic syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CD48 gene.

MONDO:1060308.text: Any inborn error of immunity in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the IRAK2 gene.

MONDO:1060309.text: Any vasculitis in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the FGR gene.

MONDO:1060310.text: Any inborn error of immunity in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the GNAI2 gene. It is characterized by midline malformations of the brain, anterior pituitary gland dysfunction, growth retardation, immunodysregulation/immunodeficiency, and skeletal defects.

MONDO:1060311.text: Any autoinflammatory syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a gain-of-function variation in the CASP1 gene. It is characterized by systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis and recurrent macrophage activation syndrome, with elevated IL-1beta and IL-18, and progressive interstitial lung disease.

MONDO:1060312.text: Any inborn error of immunity in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the STXBP3 gene. It is characterized by medically refractory infantile-onset IBD, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and, in the majority, recurrent infections.

MONDO:1060313.text: Any disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TBL1XR1 gene.

MONDO:1060314.text: An inherited susceptibility to acute infection-induced encephalitis in which the cause is a variation in the TMEFF1 gene, predisposing to herpes simplex encephalitis. Genetic TMEFF1 deficiency allows HSV-1 to rapidly enter cortical neurons.

MONDO:1060316.text: Any combined immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the RGS10 gene. It is characterized by recurrent infections, hypergammaglobulinemia, profoundly reduced lymphocyte chemotaxis, abnormal lymph node architecture, and short stature due to growth hormone deficiency.

MONDO:1060317.text: Any combined immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a biallelic germline mutation in the ASXL1 gene. It is characterized by progressive B-cell loss with hypogammaglobulinemia, recurrent pneumonia, progressive cytopenias,impaired cytotoxic T and NK cell populations, chronic macrocytosis, chronic ulcerated granulomatous skin lesions, and EBV-associated Hodgkin lymphoma. Genome-wide DNA methylation showed extensive hypomethylation, epigenetic age approximately 27 years older than chronological age, and shortened telomeres.

MONDO:1060318.text: Any immunodeficiency disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TKFC gene. It is characterized by chronic active Epstein-Barr virus disease, multiple bacterial and viral infections, hypogammaglobulinemia, near-absent natural killer cells, and decreased memory B cells, without the multisystem features of triokinase and FMN cyclase deficiency syndrome.

MONDO:1060319.text: A hereditary neoplastic syndrome caused by germline loss-of-function variation in the ELP1 gene. It is characterized by an increased risk of childhood Sonic Hedgehog (SHH)-activated medulloblastoma.

MONDO:1060320.text: Any congenital disorder of glycosylation in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the ALG2 gene. It includes congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ii and congenital myasthenic syndrome 14.

MONDO:1060321.text: Any type 1 interferonopathy in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the PTPN1 gene.

MONDO:1060322.text: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the DROSHA gene. Pathogenic germline loss-of-function variants in DROSHA confer a predisposition to pineoblastoma, usually in childhood, which may be recurrent or metastatic. Wilms tumor has also been reported. Tumors carry a somatic second variation in DROSHA.

MONDO:1060323.text: Any hereditary neurological disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the HSPD1 gene.

MONDO:1061000.text: Any tubulinopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TUBB gene. Heterozygous TUBB variants cause two overlapping developmental disorders, complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations (CDCBM) and congenital symmetric circumferential skin creases (CSCSC), also known as circumferential skin creases Kunze type. The clinical findings are diverse and include abnormalities of the cortex, basal ganglia, corpus callosum, brain stem and cerebellum, microcephaly, intellectual disability, facial dysmorphism, excess skin folding and growth retardation.

MONDO:1061001.text: An acrodermatitis characterized by the acute onset of a self-limited, symmetrical, monomorphic papular or papulovesicular eruption predominantly on the cheeks, buttocks and extensor surfaces of the extremities, with relative sparing of the trunk. It mainly affects children between 1 and 6 years of age and is considered an immunologic reaction triggered by viral infections, most commonly Epstein-Barr virus and hepatitis B virus, or occasionally by vaccination. Lesions typically resolve spontaneously within weeks without scarring.

MONDO:1061002.text: A salivary gland adenocarcinoma that arises predominantly from the minor salivary glands, most often in the palate, and rarely from the major salivary glands. It is characterized by cytologic uniformity and architectural diversity, with tumor cells showing pale to clear nuclei with inconspicuous nucleoli arranged in a wide variety of growth patterns. It commonly harbors a PRKD1 E710D mutation, typically presents as a painless, slow-growing mass, and generally has an excellent prognosis.

MONDO:7770001.text: Any spinocerebellar ataxia that occurs in horses due to a variation in the FDXR gene. EJSCA is a degenerative axonopathy characterized by acute onset of ataxia within the first month of life, affecting the pelvic limbs more severely than the thoracic limb and rapidly progressing to inability to stand.

MONDO:7770002.text: An eating disorder characterized by avoidance or restriction of food intake due to one or more of the following: lack of interest in eating or food, sensitivity to sensory characteristics of food (such as taste, texture, smell, or appearance), or concern about aversive consequences of eating (such as choking or vomiting), resulting in persistent failure to meet appropriate nutritional and/or energy needs as manifested by significant weight loss, nutritional deficiency, dependence on enteral feeding or nutritional supplements, or marked interference with psychosocial functioning, and where the eating disturbance is not better explained by lack of available food, cultural or religious practices, another mental disorder, or a concurrent medical condition.

MONDO:7770003.text: A form of diabetes mellitus unique to individuals with cystic fibrosis (CF), arising primarily from progressive fibrotic destruction of the pancreas leading to insulin deficiency, with additional contributions from insulin resistance. CFRD affects approximately 20% of adolescents and 40-50% of adults with CF. It shares features with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes but is a distinct clinical entity with its own diagnostic criteria and management guidelines.

MONDO:7770004.text: A disease associated with CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) dysfunction that does not fulfill the diagnostic criteria for cystic fibrosis (CF). CFTR-related disorders are characterized by clinical evidence of CFTR dysfunction limited to a single organ system, a sweat chloride concentration below the CF diagnostic threshold (typically less than 60 mmol/L), and CFTR genotypes that often include at least one variant not classified as CF-causing. Recognized CFTR-related disorders include congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD), acute recurrent or chronic pancreatitis, and disseminated bronchiectasis.

MONDO:7770005.text: A liver disorder that arises as a consequence of cystic fibrosis. Cystic fibrosis-related liver disease encompasses a spectrum of hepatobiliary abnormalities caused by CFTR dysfunction in cholangiocytes, including focal biliary cirrhosis, multilobular biliary cirrhosis, hepatic steatosis, and cholangiopathy. It is a significant cause of non-pulmonary morbidity and mortality in CF, affecting approximately 5-10% of CF patients.

MONDO:7770006.text: A grouping class for human diseases classified by the body system or anatomical component primarily affected.

MONDO:7770008.text: A grouping class for human diseases classified by their etiologic mechanism, encompassing primarily intrinsic (genetic, genomic), primarily extrinsic (e.g., infections, toxins, radiation), and complex multifactorial (e.g. nutritional) causes.

MONDO:7770009.text: A grouping class for human diseases caused by genetic or genomic alterations, including chromosomal abnormalities and heritable mutations.

MONDO:7770010.text: A grouping class for human diseases caused primarily by extrinsic factors, including infections, toxins, nutritional deficiencies, iatrogenic causes, and environmental exposures.

MONDO:7770011.text: A grouping class for human diseases classified by their underlying molecular or pathophysiological mechanism, such as protein aggregation, ion channel dysfunction, or signal transduction disruption.
